articles.title: Authors Can Defend Against AI Allegations With ‘Paper Trail’ Tools. Is It Enough?
articles.descEn: As the publishing industry wrestles with paranoia over the provenance of manuscripts, writers are caught in an impossible bind.
articles.titleEn: Authors Can Defend Against AI Allegations With ‘Paper Trail’ Tools. Is It Enough?
summaryLinesEn: While Pangram claims an “industry-leading” false positive rate of 0.01 percent when used on creative writing, Rasenberger said the Authors Guild has “heard of lots of instances where people have put their own human-authored work in Pangram and gotten a result back saying it was AI-generated.”

Rasenberger worries that authors are up against a climate of distrust—they should “refrain from accusations of other authors because it just does not support a healthy literary community,” she says—and overconfidence in AI detection tools, which can be fooled and have been known to produce false positives.
According to Pangram , a robust but by no means infallible AI detection tool, some 78 percent of the text was AI-generated.

Rasenberger worries that authors are up against a climate of distrust—they should “refrain from accusations of other authors because it just does not support a healthy literary community,” she says—and overconfidence in AI detection tools, which can be fooled and have been known to produce false positives.

Andrea Bartz is a prolific novelist with an impressive résumé . Since 2019, she has published five thrillers, become a New York Times bestselling author, had her work optioned by the likes of Netflix and Hulu , and picked up an endorsement from Reese Witherspoon’s influential book club.

She also has a legal claim to fame: Bartz was the lead plaintiff in a class-action suit against Anthropic that alleged the company had downloaded millions of copyrighted books from pirate sites to use as training data for its models. Anthropic last year agreed to pay $1.5 billion in the largest copyright settlement in US history .

But while Bartz and many other writers were on guard against this plunder of their work, another AI threat was brewing. What happens when authors are accused of relying on artificial intelligence themselves?

localization.title: 저자는 'Paper Trail' 도구를 사용하여 AI 주장을 방어할 수 있음 · 충분합니까
summaryLines: Pangram은 창의적인 글쓰기에 사용될 때 "업계 최고의" 오탐률이 0.01%라고 주장하지만 Rasenberger는 Authors Guild가 "사람들이 자신의 인간 저작물을 Pangram에 넣고 그것이 AI로 생성되었다는 결과를 얻은 사례를 많이 들었다"고 말함
Rasenberger는 작가들이 불신의 분위기에 직면해 있다고 걱정함 · 그들은 "건강한 문학 공동체를 지원하지 않기 때문에 다른 작가들의 비난을 삼가야 합니다"라고 그녀는 말함 · 그리고 속일 수 있고 거짓 긍정을 생성하는 것으로 알려진 AI 탐지 도구에 대한 과신이 있음
강력하지만 결코 오류가 없는 AI 탐지 도구인 Pangram에 따르면 텍스트의 약 78%가 AI에서 생성됨

articles.title: Nvidia espionage scandal weakens Huang's lobby against tighter AI chip export controls
articles.descEn: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to an extramarital affair with a woman US intelligence agencies classify as a suspected Chinese informant. The board has launched an independent investigation. The affair weakens Huang's lobbying efforts against stricter AI chip export controls, with a newly elected Democratic Congress poised to ramp up scrutiny of AI chip smuggling to China and push for tighter restrictions.

articles.title: The climate case for AI has not been made
articles.descEn: AI leaders claim their tech will fix the climate. The evidence mostly points in the opposite direction so far.
articles.titleEn: The climate case for AI has not been made
summaryLinesEn: At this point it would be surprising if the sector even manages to zero out its climate pollution: Emissions associated with global data centers (which may handle AI as well as non-AI computing tasks) could exceed 300 million tons annually in 2035, according to the IEA’s base forecast .
CATL—which controls roughly 40% of the global market for electric-vehicle batteries—launched an AI system trained on more than 100,000 battery design cases and 600 terabytes of test data.

A peer-reviewed study published last year, led by researchers at the London School of Economics’ Grantham Research Institute and the firm Systemiq, estimated that AI could help cut global emissions by the equivalent of 3.2 to 5.4 billion tons of carbon dioxide annually by 2035—roughly on par with the US’s annual energy-related emissions on the high end, even after subtracting AI’s own energy footprint.

AI leaders claim their tech will fix the climate. The evidence mostly points in the opposite direction so far.

This week, as countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the United Nations climate conference, one topic likely to dominate the conversation is artificial intelligence. The host has already called on countries to commit to ensuring that AI is designed, powered, and deployed in ways that support climate action.

But so far, industries around the world aren’t doing nearly enough to harness the technology to actually drive down the greenhouse-gas emissions heating up the planet, despite some very optimistic claims from AI companies.

localization.title: AI에 대한 기후 사례는 아직 만들어지지 않았음
summaryLines: 현 시점에서 해당 부문이 기후 오염을 완전히 제거할 수 있다면 놀라운 일이 될 것임 · IEA의 기본 예측에 따르면 글로벌 데이터 센터(AI 및 비AI 컴퓨팅 작업을 처리할 수 있음)와 관련된 배출량은 2035년에 연간 3억 톤을 초과할 수 있음
전 세계 전기 자동차 배터리 시장의 약 40%를 장악하고 있는 CATL은 100,000개 이상의 배터리 설계 사례와 600테라바이트의 테스트 데이터를 학습한 AI 시스템을 출시함

런던 정경대학(London School of Economics)의 Grantham Research Institute와 Systemiq 회사의 연구자들이 주도한 동료 검토 연구에서는 AI가 2035년까지 연간 32억~54억 톤에 달하는 이산화탄소 배출량을 줄이는 데 도움이 될 수 있다고 추정함 · 이는 AI의 자체 에너지 발자국을 차감한 후에도 미국의 연간 에너지 관련 배출량과 대략 비슷한 수준임

articles.title: 令和7年度厚生労働省 老人保健健康増進等事業・社会福祉推進事業・障害者総合福祉推進事業
articles.titleEn: 令和7年度厚生労働省 老人保健健康増進等事業・社会福祉推進事業・障害者総合福祉推進事業
summaryLinesEn: BCP 作成を行動に変える、平時の体制整備ハンドブック～災害への備えと「対話」～ （前半）令和7年度 社会福祉推進事業 医療扶助における多剤・重複投薬対策等の効果的かつ効率的な実施方法等に関する調査研究 報告書 （後半）令和7年度 社会福祉推進事業 医療扶助における多剤・重複投薬対策等の効果的かつ効率的な実施方法等に関する調査研究 報告書 令和7年度 障害者総合福祉推進事業 共同生活援助の質の確保のための（自立支援）協議会の役割等に関する実態調査 報告書
（株）野村総合研究所では、厚生労働省の補助金を受けて、老人保健健康増進等事業・社会福祉推進事業・障害者総合福祉推進事業として下記の調査研究を実施しました。
本調査研究事業は、福祉事務所が実施する被保護者健康管理支援事業等の実態把握を行うとともに、「被保護者健康管理支援事業の手引き（第2版）」の改定方策を検討すること、同時に、令和7年度より始まった都道府県による市町村支援の実施実態等を把握すること等を目的として実施した。

articles.title: 減少する児童館の新たな役割
articles.titleEn: 減少する児童館の新たな役割
summaryLinesEn: 担い手が多様化するなかで、公的施設である児童館が、地域でどのような役割を果たすのかが、あらためて問われている。
一方、児童館の数は2006年の4,718館をピークに減少し、24年には4,248館となった。
2023年12月に「こどもの居場所づくりに関する指針」が閣議決定されるなど、こどもの居場所づくりは政策として推進され、こども食堂や学習支援の場など、NPOや地域住民が担う多様な居場所が全国で広がっている。

articles.descEn: Explore APAC’s 2026 shopping seasons, from Singles’ Day to Diwali, Lunar New Year, and Ramadan. See app and ad trends, standout markets & categories.
articles.titleEn: 2026 APAC Shopping Season Playbook
summaryLinesEn: Global shopping app downloads are forecast to reach 6.43 billion in 2026 , remaining above 6 billion for a fourth consecutive year.

China shows a different pattern: mid-year activity overlaps with the 618 festival, and the 2026 forecast peaks in October, within the broader Golden Week and Singles’ Day promotional window, before easing.
These differences support planning around multiple local shopping occasions rather than applying one year-end campaign calendar across the region.

sourceContent.headline: 2026 APAC Shopping Season Playbook
sourceContent.description: Explore APAC’s 2026 shopping seasons, from Singles’ Day to Diwali, Lunar New Year, and Ramadan. See app and ad trends, standout markets & categories.
paragraphs: Global shopping app downloads are forecast to reach 6.43 billion in 2026 , remaining above 6 billion for a fourth consecutive year.

China shows a different pattern: mid-year activity overlaps with the 618 festival, and the 2026 forecast peaks in October, within the broader Golden Week and Singles’ Day promotional window, before easing.
These differences support planning around multiple local shopping occasions rather than applying one year-end campaign calendar across the region.

Global shopping app downloads are forecast to reach 6.43 billion in 2026 , remaining above 6 billion for a fourth consecutive year. After several years of growth, downloads have leveled off, suggesting acquisition is stabilizing as mobile shopping becomes a familiar part of consumers’ digital routines. Smartphones have made it easier to browse and shop across settings, reducing the effort required to access retailers.

Total Sessions are projected to exceed 3 trillion in 2026 , with a five-year CAGR of 6.6% —more than twice the rate for downloads. The gap points to continued growth in app use, as consumers return to shopping platforms more often. Retailers can respond by focusing on relevant offers, straightforward product discovery, and a smooth path to checkout.

Asia is the largest region for shopping app downloads, with about 2.6 billion forecast in 2026, up 2% year over year. India accounts for 40% of that total, followed by China’s iOS market at 19% and Southeast Asia at 18%. North America has the fastest download growth, at 6%, while downloads decline in Europe and Latin America.

articles.title: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production
articles.descEn: NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models.
articles.titleEn: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production
summaryLinesEn: Optimized for NVIDIA B200 GPUs, these recipes take the guesswork out of deployment, delivering up to 2x performance out of the box.
They help developers bring Korea’s open models into production faster and turn them into broadly accessible AI for All services.

NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom , K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research , Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies .

paragraphs: Optimized for NVIDIA B200 GPUs, these recipes take the guesswork out of deployment, delivering up to 2x performance out of the box.

NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom , K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research , Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies .
As models grow beyond the capacity of a single GPU, they must be split across multiple GPUs, requiring careful coordination of request routing and communication to maintain performance.

NVIDIA Dynamo is an open source, distributed inference-serving framework built to deploy models in multi-node environments at data center scale. It handles this routing and communication to maximize inference performance.

articles.title: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration
articles.descEn: NVIDIA and Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) are expanding their collaboration across the country’s sovereign AI ecosystem, from AI semiconductors and data center infrastructure to talent, startups, models, agents and security.
articles.titleEn: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration
summaryLinesEn: NVIDIA and Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) are expanding their collaboration across the country’s sovereign AI ecosystem, from AI semiconductors and data center infrastructure to talent, startups, models, agents and security.

The collaboration lays the groundwork for Korean NPU and XPU companies to explore participation in the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem, and includes NVIDIA training and certification programs, hackathons and technical seminars to strengthen GPU utilization.

Through Korea’s AI for All initiative, NVIDIA will collaborate with three selected consortia and four leading Korean foundation model builders, using NVIDIA Dynamo software to optimize and scale AI inference.
articles.summary:
NVIDIA and Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) are expanding their collaboration across the country’s sovereign AI ecosystem, from AI semiconductors and data center infrastructure to talent, startups, models, agents and security.
The collaboration lays the groundwork for Korean NPU and XPU companies to explore participation in the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem, and includes NVIDIA training and certification programs, hackathons and technical seminars to strengthen GPU utilization.
Through Korea’s AI for All initiative, NVIDIA will collaborate with three selected consortia and four leading Korean foundation model builders, using NVIDIA Dynamo software to optimize and scale AI inference.

articles.title: Korea’s AI Ecosystem Advances and Secures Agentic AI With NVIDIA
articles.descEn: Hyundai Motor Group and AIM Intelligence explore NVIDIA NemoClaw and OpenShell for secure enterprise agents, and LG AI Research opens API for ‘K-EXAONE-2.5’ trained on Nemotron datasets.
articles.titleEn: Korea’s AI Ecosystem Advances and Secures Agentic AI With NVIDIA
summaryLinesEn: Nemotron-Personas-Korea is an open dataset of 7 million fully synthetic Korean personas, grounded in official Korean statistics, that model builders use to ground training data and evaluation in Korean contexts.
As AI agents take on more work, they need capable open models and security that advances alongside them.
On the model side, LG AI Research is opening application programming interface access for K-EXAONE-2.5, developed using NVIDIA Nemotron datasets, including Nemotron-Personas-Korea .

sourceContent.description: Hyundai Motor Group and AIM Intelligence explore NVIDIA NemoClaw and OpenShell for secure enterprise agents, and LG AI Research opens API for ‘K-EXAONE-2.5’ trained on Nemotron datasets.
paragraphs: Nemotron-Personas-Korea is an open dataset of 7 million fully synthetic Korean personas, grounded in official Korean statistics, that model builders use to ground training data and evaluation in Korean contexts.
As AI agents take on more work, they need capable open models and security that advances alongside them.
On the model side, LG AI Research is opening application programming interface access for K-EXAONE-2.5, developed using NVIDIA Nemotron datasets, including Nemotron-Personas-Korea .

Hyundai Motor Group is exploring NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and the NVIDIA OpenShell runtime, while AIM Intelligence is integrating its Starfort platform with NVIDIA OpenShell to support secure AI agents for employee productivity and enterprise workflows .

A key component of the NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform, OpenShell provides a secure runtime with sandboxed execution and policy-based controls to safeguard sensitive data, manage access to enterprise tools and govern autonomous agent actions.

articles.titleEn: NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum
summaryLinesEn: NVIDIA also announced an investment in Korean startup Point2 , with additional investments planned in Motif Technologies , RLWRLD and Upstage.

The planned investments build on NVIDIA’s work with Korea’s startup and venture community, including more than 1,000 Korea-based members of NVIDIA Inception , a program that helps startups grow with access to preferred pricing, technical expertise and opportunities for investor introductions.

Point2 Technology, an AI interconnect company, builds scalable, radio frequency-based interconnects that move data between chips and racks in AI factories, offering an innovative alternative to conventional copper and optical interconnect solutions for AI cluster scale-up, delivering the reach, performance and efficiency needed for next-generation AI infrastructure.

sourceContent.headline: A comprehensive guide to understanding Arm Neoverse
sourceContent.description: Learn how Arm Neoverse powers cloud infrastructure, data centers, AI systems and high-performance computing at scale.
paragraphs: Cloud platforms now operate across global regions where AI workloads demand greater memory bandwidth and sustained performance.
Designed to power the next generation of AI infrastructure, it reflects the broader shift towards agentic AI workloads that demand sustained performance at massive scale.
Meanwhile, the Cobalt 200 , built on Neoverse CSS V3, extends performance density and energy efficiency for next-generation cloud environments.

A decade ago, cloud infrastructure was dominated by web applications and enterprise workloads with relatively predictable performance and power profiles. Today, it must scale artificial intelligence (AI) workloads, secure multi-tenant environments, and distribute compute beyond the data center and closer to where data is created.

Cloud platforms now operate across global regions where AI workloads demand greater memory bandwidth and sustained performance. At the same time, distributed systems push compute closer to users and machines, while operators face mounting pressure to improve performance-per-watt, strengthen architectural security, and shorten time to deployment.
Infrastructure has become increasingly distributed, software-defined, and AI-enabled and must deliver high performance while scaling efficiently within fixed power and cost constraints.

articles.descEn: Introducing the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2: a new proprietary evaluation, updated benchmarks, and a headline metric that rewards model calibration
articles.titleEn: Introducing the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2
summaryLinesEn: We test 120 questions with variations such as reordered options, swapped labels, and negated yes/no questions, then measure how consistent the model’s probabilities are across those variations ➤ AA-Omniscience-Decision v1.1 and HLE-MultiChoice v1.1 (15% each, down from 25%): AA-Omniscience-Decision now varies the wording of its “I don’t know” option across ten alternatives.

➤ Three decision models sit within 1 point at the top of the Index: Drex Max v1.1 from Nace AI and GLiDE v1.2 from Fastino Labs both score 73, with Mammoth 27B from Base Labs scoring 72 ➤ Cost per 1M Tasks varies by more than 60x across decision models: Celeris-1.1 Decision ($14), Decider v1.2 ($68) and Drex Max v1.1 ($102) sit on the Decision Index vs.

This means GLiDE v1.2 costs $780, nearly 8x higher than Drex Max v1.1 despite only 33% higher list prices ➤ Language models can score higher, alongside higher Cost and Time per Task: Claude Haiku 5.5 (Max) scores 77 and GPT-6 Luna (Max) scores 76 on Decision Index v2, putting them ~3 points ahead of Drex Max v1.1.

articles.title: Don't like Google Health's AI Coach? Here's how to turn it off - Engadget
articles.descEn: If this Premium feature is bugging you, there's good news: you aren't stuck with it.
articles.titleEn: Don't like Google Health's AI Coach? Here's how to turn it off - Engadget
summaryLinesEn: Select Your data in Google Health then scroll down to Feature privacy controls and select Manage feature privacy controls .

If you don't like Google Health's AI Coach or need a break from its constant advice, the easiest way to get rid of it is to cancel your Google Health Premium subscription, since AI Coach does not come with the free Google Health tier.

Don't worry, because there is a way to keep Google Health Premium but temporarily (or permanently) set aside the Gemini-powered AI Coach in the app settings thanks to an update released in August 2026.

paragraphs: Select Your data in Google Health then scroll down to Feature privacy controls and select Manage feature privacy controls .

If you don't like Google Health's AI Coach or need a break from its constant advice, the easiest way to get rid of it is to cancel your Google Health Premium subscription, since AI Coach does not come with the free Google Health tier.

Don't worry, because there is a way to keep Google Health Premium but temporarily (or permanently) set aside the Gemini-powered AI Coach in the app settings thanks to an update released in August 2026.

If you don't like Google Health's AI Coach or need a break from its constant advice, the easiest way to get rid of it is to cancel your Google Health Premium subscription, since AI Coach does not come with the free Google Health tier. But what if you just want to hide it for a bit and continue to enjoy the other benefits of Google Health Premium? These include personalized sleep summaries, advanced sleep tracking algorithms, Sleep Score, Health Guardian that tracks noticeable changes in health and wellness , cycle predictions, nutrition tracking and more.

Don't worry, because there is a way to keep Google Health Premium but temporarily (or permanently) set aside the Gemini-powered AI Coach in the app settings thanks to an update released in August 2026. It's a simple matter of going to your privacy controls and toggling the feature off. And you can turn it back on again any time you want.

In the Google Health app while subscribed to Google Health Premium, tap your profile photo in the top right corner. Select Your data in Google Health then scroll down to Feature privacy controls and select Manage feature privacy controls . Select Google Health Coach and the Turn off button. That's it! You can also go to your profile photo > Google Health settings > Coaching , and turn off Health Coach from there. Another option is to change Coach messages on Today from Standard to No Coach insights , which will only show basic updates and no messages.

articles.title: I Used NYT Cooking’s New AI-Powered Recipe Modifier, and It’s Actually Pretty Good
articles.descEn: The New York Times has added a beta feature to its Cooking app that helps readers swap ingredients or adjust recipes to suit their needs. It mostly hits the mark.
articles.titleEn: I Used NYT Cooking’s New AI-Powered Recipe Modifier, and It’s Actually Pretty Good
summaryLinesEn: The Times doesn't share Cooking's subscriber numbers, but NYT executive communications director Jordan Cohen said the site and app were visited 514 million times in 2025, and its YouTube channel has over 1.4 million subscribers.

Earlier this year, the Times allowed AI to help with a recipe-scaling feature (modifying ingredient quantities so "serves 4" turns into "serves 6") and converting from imperial measurements to metric—cups, tablespoons, and Fahrenheit to grams, milliliters, and Celsius.

It thought about it for a moment—"simmering" in AI Cooking patois—and then offered up "Chicken Breast and Dumplings," with the "breast" in the title rendered in the red-orange color that indicates a modification.

It thought about it for a moment—"simmering" in AI Cooking patois—and then offered up "Chicken Breast and Dumplings," with the "breast" in the title rendered in the red-orange color that indicates a modification.

In an aside in the New York Times Cooking video I watched recently, where Melissa Clark made her lemony white bean soup with turkey and greens , the food reporter and recipe columnist invited viewers to leave a comment telling her what they do with the kale stems. It highlighted this sweet, funny relationship between a media brand’s personalities and its audience, a warm-casual vibe.

I am not among the multitudes in the Cooking section's commenter army, but a few days later I was very surprised to see some of them in open revolt. I was even more surprised to see why: In an iOS-only beta, the Times is now using AI to allow subscribers to modify recipes.
Below the article announcing the change on October 23, commenters loudly aired their grievances, threatening to cancel subscriptions, asking who wanted this, and how to turn it off.

articles.title: Andrej Karpathy built a curated video platform in a weekend using Claude and 20 years of Hacker News
articles.descEn: OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy used Claude's Opus 5.5 to filter 43 million Hacker News comments into 6,454 curated videos. The result beats YouTube's own recommendations, he says.
articles.titleEn: Andrej Karpathy built a curated video platform in a weekend using Claude and 20 years of Hacker News
summaryLinesEn: Claude filtered 43 million comments from 20 years of Hacker News and distilled them into 6,454 videos that keep getting recommended there .
The site needs no login, shows a single mid-video frame instead of optimized thumbnails, and stores state locally in the browser.
Andrej Karpathy, OpenAI co-founder and current Anthropic AI researcher, built HackerTube over a weekend using Claude's Opus 5.5 model.

Andrej Karpathy, OpenAI co-founder and current Anthropic AI researcher, built HackerTube over a weekend using Claude's Opus 5.5 model. Claude filtered 43 million comments from 20 years of Hacker News and distilled them into 6,454 videos that keep getting recommended there . The result is a "significantly better viewing experience" than YouTube's own recommendations, Karpathy writes on X . The site needs no login, shows a single mid-video frame instead of optimized thumbnails, and stores state locally in the browser. Right after, Karpathy built TristanTube , "one-shotted with Claude Code in 3 minutes," with 47,000 videos drawn from a YouTube channel list by Tristan Hume.

Karpathy says he let Claude Code handle nearly all the work, from data analysis to server setup. His only manual steps were a Google Cloud API key, a rented server, and buying the domain. Projects that used to take weeks can now be done in a few hours, Karpathy says.

8일 업계에 따르면 KT는 이같은 내용을 골자로 하는 마이AI 고도화 로드맵을 세웠다.
마이AI는 14개의 영역별 특화 에이전트로 구성된 마이케이티의 핵심 AI 기술이다.

KT가 고객 앱 '마이케이티'의 인공지능(AI) 에이전트 '마이AI'를 상담·추천을 넘어 고객 요청을 스스로 판단해 처리하는 실행형 에이전트로 고도화한다. 맞춤 추천 엔진과 멀티 에이전트 오케스트레이터 기술을 앞세워 조회·상담 중심이던 고객 앱을 AI가 제안부터 실행까지 맡는 초개인화 채널로 바꾼다는 구상이다. 8일 업계에 따르면 KT는 이같은 내용을 골자로 하는 마이AI 고도화 로드맵을 세웠다. 마이AI는 14개의 영역별 특화 에이전트로 구성된 마이케이티의 핵심 AI 기술이다. 사용자 요청을 이해해 최적의 답변과 추천을 제공한다. 마이케이티에 도입 이후 약 한달간 AI 이용자 수는 5배, 고객당 AI 발화수는 7배 이상 늘었다. KT 마이AI는 무선에 한정됐던 요금제 추천을 연내 유선·결합상품까지 넓힌다. 단순 요금제 안내를 넘어 고객이 가입한 상품과 할인·결합 혜택, 실납부액을 종합 반영한 맞춤형 추천 기능을 정교화한다는 목표다. 내년 1분기에는 자율 판단·실행 단계에 들어간다. AI가 응답 적합성을 평가해 최적 에이전트를 배정하고, 고객 의도에 맞는 서비스 제공을 위한 업무별 통제 장치를 적용한다. 부가서비스에 그쳤던 AI를 통한 직접가입 역시 고객 반응과 안정성을 고려해 처리 범위 확대를 단계적으로 검토한다. 2분기에는 초개인화 서비스로 진화한다. 추천 대상을 요금제에서 KT 멤버십 혜택과 장기혜택쿠폰 등으로 넓히고, 고객이 메뉴와 혜택을 직접 찾지 않아도 상황에 맞는 서비스를 안내받도록 한다는 구상이다. 기술 핵심은 '마이 AI 오케스트레이터'다. 14개 전문 에이전트를 조율하는 엔진으로, 고객의 복합 의도와 맥락을 분석해 실행 계획을 세우고 여러 에이전트의 협업을 이끈다. 모호한 질문에는 유형별 탐침으로 구체적 선택지를 제시하고, 대화 이력을 바탕으로 질의를 재작성한다. 요금제 추천에는 딥러닝 추천 모델 'DeepFM'을 적용했다. 데이터·음성·문자 사용량, 온라인동영상서비스(OTT) 이용, 약정·기기변경 이력 등 이용 패턴을 학습한다. 여기에 추천엔진 '인텔리디시전'을 결합해 요금제 전환 예측과 대화 맥락을 실시간 반영한다. 상품 추천뿐 아니라 의도파악, 의미 기반 취향 이해, 상호작용형 추천이 가능하다. KT 마이AI 모델은 답변 품질과 서비스 안정성을 고려해 GPT 계열을 적용했다. 자체 AI 모델 '믿음'은 향후 모두의 AI와 마이케이티에 순차 적용할 계획이다. KT는 최적요금제 고지 의무에도 마이AI 모델을 활용을 검토한다. KT 관계자는 “최적요금제 세부 운영 방식은 현재 검토 중으로 마이AI와의 연계 여부를 포함한 구체적 사항은 향후 고객 편의성을 높이는 방향으로 반영할 예정”이라고 말했다. 박준호 기자 junho@etnews.com

AI가 응답 적합성을 평가해 최적 에이전트를 배정하고, 고객 의도에 맞는 서비스 제공을 위한 업무별 통제 장치를 적용한다. 부가서비스에 그쳤던 AI를 통한 직접가입 역시 고객 반응과 안정성을 고려해 처리 범위 확대를 단계적으로 검토한다. 2분기에는 초개인화 서비스로 진화한다. 추천 대상을 요금제에서 KT 멤버십 혜택과 장기혜택쿠폰 등으로 넓히고, 고객이 메뉴와 혜택을 직접 찾지 않아도 상황에 맞는 서비스를 안내받도록 한다는 구상이다. 기술 핵심은 '마이 AI 오케스트레이터'다. 14개 전문 에이전트를 조율하는 엔진으로, 고객의 복합 의도와 맥락을 분석해 실행 계획을 세우고 여러 에이전트의 협업을 이끈다. 모호한 질문에는 유형별 탐침으로 구체적 선택지를 제시하고, 대화 이력을 바탕으로 질의를 재작성한다. 요금제 추천에는 딥러닝 추천 모델 'DeepFM'을 적용했다. 데이터·음성·문자 사용량, 온라인동영상서비스(OTT) 이용, 약정·기기변경 이력 등 이용 패턴을 학습한다. 여기에 추천엔진 '인텔리디시전'을 결합해 요금제 전환 예측과 대화 맥락을 실시간 반영한다. 상품 추천뿐 아니라 의도파악, 의미 기반 취향 이해, 상호작용형 추천이 가능하다. KT 마이AI 모델은 답변 품질과 서비스 안정성을 고려해 GPT 계열을 적용했다. 자체 AI 모델 '믿음'은 향후 모두의 AI와 마이케이티에 순차 적용할 계획이다. KT는 최적요금제 고지 의무에도 마이AI 모델을 활용을 검토한다. KT 관계자는 “최적요금제 세부 운영 방식은 현재 검토 중으로 마이AI와의 연계 여부를 포함한 구체적 사항은 향후 고객 편의성을 높이는 방향으로 반영할 예정”이라고 말했다. 박준호 기자 junho@etnews.com

articles.title: The biggest disadvantages of using AI glasses - Engadget
articles.descEn: Despite the benefit to the disabled and aging communities, smart glasses are problematic when it comes to privacy and safety concerns. Here's what to watch for.
articles.titleEn: The biggest disadvantages of using AI glasses - Engadget
summaryLinesEn: A 2026 survey conducted by Security.org found that 25 percent of respondents reported that they were likely to buy a pair of smart glasses in the coming year.

Some seniors have shown a strong interest in them, adopting the technology for their accessibility features and showing interest in how well they can help one keep track of doctor visits or medication reminders.
If you've spent any amount of time scrolling YouTube or a social media platform that has shorts or reels of some kind, you've likely seen a content creator using smart glasses.

There are a few reasons to hesitate before buying a pair.

The world of AI glasses, or smart glasses as they're perhaps more commonly known, has been a truly fascinating one to watch develop. What once felt like something out of a classic science fiction film — that of a pair of glasses with technology and cutting-edge hardware built directly into them — has become one of a very plausible, and altogether expensive, reality.

On the one hand, it's always fun to see how technology evolves and improves over time. On the other, it's a piece of technology that has some rather alarming history attached to it, as well as some incredibly valid concerns about its future .

articles.descEn: Groups that own the music rights to Elvis Presley and Eminem’s tracks filed the latest lawsuits.
articles.titleEn: Suno AI music generator sued again for copyright infringement - Engadget
summaryLinesEn: It recently filed a lawsuit against Anthropic , claiming $41 million in damages for allegedly training its AI models on the musician's works without permission.
New lawsuits are claiming that Suno has once again committed copyright infringement by using Elvis Presley and Eminem's likeness to create AI-generated songs.

As first reported by Variety , a group that owns the rights to Presley's music and Eight Mile Style, a music publishing company that owns hundreds of Eminem recordings, filed separate lawsuits against Suno.

Groups that own the music rights to Elvis Presley and Eminem’s tracks filed the latest lawsuits.

New lawsuits are claiming that Suno has once again committed copyright infringement by using Elvis Presley and Eminem's likeness to create AI-generated songs. As first reported by Variety , a group that owns the rights to Presley's music and Eight Mile Style, a music publishing company that owns hundreds of Eminem recordings, filed separate lawsuits against Suno. Both lawsuits offered examples of songs created through the AI music generator that allegedly sound like Presley or mimic Eminem's lyrics.

A group of attorneys representing the plaintiffs in each case said that Suno's actions "make human creativity obsolete, coldly replicating without a license in seconds what takes years to learn, struggle with, maintain, and endlessly attempt to make better and perfect." Suno countered with a statement to Variety that said it doesn't allow "any unauthorized use of an artist's work," specifying that it prohibits using "specific artists' names and songs," while also working with third-party companies to screen for "potential misuse."

summaryLinesEn: Hodgkin and Huxley’s approach can be broken down into three steps, and most scientific modeling involves some version of them.

AI for Science grantees Jakob Macke , Daniel Gedon , and Stefan Wahl are researchers at the ELLIS Institute Tübingen and the University of Tübingen, where they build AI tools for developing scientific models in neuroscience and beyond. In this guest post, they discuss how AI is starting to change scientific modeling.
Science Nov 4, 2026 Investigating vault particles with Claude

In 1951, Cambridge University’s computer went out of action for six months. This was inconvenient for physiologist Andrew Huxley, who, alongside his colleague Alan Hodgkin, had just built a set of equations to describe how a particular squid nerve cell fired. The scientists wanted to understand the “action potential” of these nerve cells: the electrical pulses they use to communicate, which underlie everything brains do, from perception to intelligence. The only way to find out whether the equations worked was to solve them and compare the solutions to data.

summaryLinesEn: But then on Thursday, tech stocks almost across the board plunged back down even more for a collective loss of $2.5 trillion in market cap — the Nasdaq fell more than 5.5% — on more generalized worries that, well, the AI boom could slow.

The day after the elections, stocks of many tech companies shot up, a bit paradoxically because investors apparently believe potential limits on AI and data centers could tamp down spending on compute and thus improve tech company margins that have made investors nervous.

Here’s all of this week’s enterprise and emerging tech news, analysis and commentary from SiliconANGLE and beyond: Amazon, Microsoft and other tech giants close higher after Democrats’ midterm sweep No, data centers won’t get shut down, and AI will continue apace — just regulated as it needs to be, and we can hope it’s in the right way to protect people and communities and innovation all at the same time.

Midterm elections will put AI and data centers on trial, but will Big Tech end up winning anyway?

It may be a little soon to determine the ultimate winners and losers among enterprise suppliers after the midterm elections, but the early line is: Big Tech wins and data center suppliers operators such as chipmakers and neoclouds lose. Or will everybody lose?

The day after the elections, stocks of many tech companies shot up, a bit paradoxically because investors apparently believe potential limits on AI and data centers could tamp down spending on compute and thus improve tech company margins that have made investors nervous. But then on Thursday, tech stocks almost across the board plunged back down even more for a collective loss of $2.5 trillion in market cap — the Nasdaq fell more than 5.5% — on more generalized worries that, well, the AI boom could slow. Suffice to say, investors are still sorting things out.

paragraphs: TE Connectivity has scaled Connect Decisions to 2,000 planners, but Connect Talent reached general availability only in September and has early customers in deployment.
The lessons from that success are now the blueprint for the expanded Amazon Connect family : Connect Customer, Connect Talent, Connect Health and Connect Decisions.
“I worry that people start trying to come up with new metrics to measure the impact of AI, but it’s the same metrics,” she explained.
AWS’ Colleen Aubrey: Stop inventing new AI metrics — it’s your business metrics that matter

There isn’t a business or information technology leader today who doesn’t have artificial intelligence at the top of their priority list. The challenge for most organizations is deciding what to measure and how to determine whether an AI initiative was successful.
To better understand how customers should approach AI metrics, I spoke with Colleen Aubrey from Amazon Web Services Inc ,, who has some deep experience in this area.

Security researchers have discovered hundreds of copies of a Chinese-made AI hacking tool publicly exposed to the internet for anyone to access, potentially allowing outsiders to launch cyberattacks against unsuspecting targets.

The hacking software, called Artex, is an open source autonomous penetration testing tool, meaning software that automatically probes computer systems for weaknesses, and it’s been linked to several cyberattacks since its public release in July. As open source software, it’s free for anyone to download and run on their own servers, making it a popular tool for those who cannot access Anthropic or OpenAI’s most advanced cybersecurity AI models for discovering security vulnerabilities. Microsoft has previously described Artex as a system of AI agents that can conduct cyberattacks “from reconnaissance through data exfiltration with little needed human interaction.”

In a blog post , cybersecurity firm Censys, which scans the internet for exposed or vulnerable systems, said that it identified more than 800 distinct deployments of Artex that were accessible from the web without needing a password to log in.

articles.title: Investigating vault particles with Claude
articles.descEn: We’re sharing another finding from Anthropic’s biology research lab: the first 3D structure of a vault particle found in prokaryotic cells.
articles.titleEn: Investigating vault particles with Claude
summaryLinesEn: We began by using Claude Science to search for the vault protein’s relatives across a database of about 15 billion predicted proteins.
We moved the best performers into living E. coli bacteria, where 15 of 24 produced soluble protein.
We took the project on anyway, because Claude could make up for what we didn’t know and rapidly perform analyses that would otherwise have taken us much longer.

Another such enigma is the vault particle .

Premium PC and console gaming grew again in H1 2026 as action pulled premium Steam hours ahead of shooters, US social ad budgets remained concentrated on Meta and YouTube, and GTA VI showed how a single media moment can move pre-orders. Sensor Tower’s Gaming Deep Dive: Premium PC/Console report is a front row seat for everything Steam, PlayStation, and Xbox.

Premium PC and console gaming is often described as flat. The H1 2026 numbers tell a quieter story: paid units are up, engagement is shifting by genre, and the biggest marketing dollars still cluster in a few places. For publishers and marketers planning against GTA VI and a crowded fall slate, the useful question is not whether the category moved, but where the growth, playtime, and ad attention actually went. Sensor Tower's latest Gaming Deep Dive report dives into the latest premium PC and console trends.

summaryLinesEn: ToyBlocks scales data generation through generating and executing hundreds of such plans in parallel on a single graphics processing unit (GPU), reaching up to 24 times real-time performance.

During the episode, the agent muses, “I need to figure out whether pick-and-place naturally straightens orientation or if I need to correct it manually… I have 63 calls left, plenty to run a controlled test” (0:06).

Johannes Hermle*, Ben Jones*, Lukas Althoff*, Ryan Heller, Thomas Lyttelton, Carolyn Stein, Nathan Wilmers, Maxim Massenkoff, Peter McCrory

What we measure. AI could speed up scientific discovery, but by how much depends on what AI can do and how scientists use it. Using privacy-preserving methods, we study 207,000 Claude and Claude Code research sessions to understand how Claude is used across scientific fields and research tasks. We are conducting this research to help the public better understand the state of AI for science today and assess the impact that AI may have on scientific discovery in the future.

A year ago, NVIDIA open sourced its Aerial wireless software , joining Sionna and a broader suite of open source tools for accelerating next-generation 6G network development. Together, they give researchers a foundation for testing ideas, comparing results and building on each other’s work — connecting simulation and AI training with experiments on real over-the-air wireless systems.

Today, researchers and developers are using these tools to build 6G-ready networks that do more than just transmit data — receiving signals more effectively, keeping robots and autonomous systems connected when it matters most, and adapting in real time as devices move through the world.

articles.titleEn: Extend Claude Code to remote sessions on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with security controls | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: Amazon Bedrock doesn’t use your content to train models or share it with model providers, and providers can’t access your prompts, completions, or the Amazon Bedrock service logs.

Claude Code reviews the result with Claude Opus and can send it back to planning for another attempt, up to three attempts in total.

You might already run Claude Code locally on your laptop, backed by Amazon Bedrock. This post shows how to go a step further: run it as a remote agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. The sample uses AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, so every task runs in its own isolated session inside your AWS account. You offload a coding task, close the laptop, and come back to the result.

We first discuss why teams choose Amazon Bedrock for Claude Code and highlight a few key security characteristics. Then, we discuss the remote agent architecture and walk through an accompanying sample, sample-remote-coding-agent , that implements it. The sample runs each task in its own AgentCore runtime session and returns a GitHub pull request for you to review and merge. Along the way, we show how the Amazon Bedrock data controls stay intact when a task runs remotely.

Customers choose Amazon Bedrock as Claude Code’s model provider for many reasons. These include billing and credits through their existing AWS account with no per-seat licenses, audit logging in AWS CloudTrail, and geographic inference profiles for data residency. Taxbit is a digital-asset tax and accounting compliance platform. Founded in 2018, Taxbit helps enterprises such as exchanges, payment services, and brokers calculate gains and losses, collect tax documentation, and file information returns at scale. Now, a cited, permission-aware AI assistant helps compliance teams find answers right inside the product dashboard.

But the knowledge needed to use that dashboard well was scattered across the public website, API documentation, and help-center articles, and a meaningful share was never written down at all. When a customer asked “what does this form status mean?”, they either went digging or filed a support ticket. Today more than 55 percent of users who ask Assist a question return to ask another within 24 hours, according to Taxbit’s internal production analytics.

In this post, we share how we built Taxbit Assist , the AI assistant now embedded in the Taxbit dashboard, on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore , a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. We cover the architecture, the retrieval work that made answers trustworthy enough to ship to regulated customers, how we handle safety and data residency, and how we continuously measure answer quality on live production traffic.

sourceContent.headline: The freed-up analyst: how AI leverage becomes a sourcing advantage
sourceContent.description: Discover how AI frees analyst capacity for deal sourcing in banking. Learn why governed AI and compliance guardrails turn freed time into won mandates.
paragraphs: Deloitte estimated that generative AI could lift front-office productivity at the world’s largest investment banks by 27% to 35% by 2026, adding roughly $3.5 million in additional revenue per front-office employee.
Solomon’s example captures the shift happening across investment banking.

( Business Insider ) When every employee can delegate work to teams of agents, the question shifts from how many analysts you need to what team members, from junior to senior, should focus on with the time that is now freed up.

There’s a number that defines the economics of every investment banking team: one. That’s about how many deals a banker supports per year in a traditionally staffed team. JPMorgan discovered this the hard way when it found that fewer than 30% of its bankers had five or more active clients , amounting to about one deal per banker. This number is the result of a staffing pyramid that has existed for decades, with layers of analysts doing the production work that keeps a deal moving, topped by a thin tier of senior bankers who own the client relationship and the judgment.

As AI agents become capable junior co-workers, this pyramid is being dismantled . David Solomon, Goldman Sachs CEO, described what used to happen when a company prepared to go public: a team of about half a dozen people would spend two weeks drafting an S-1, the regulatory prospectus that details a business, its financials, and its risk factors. Now, Solomon said, AI can get that document 95% of the way there in a few minutes. If the 95% is “now a commodity,” he said, the remaining 5% matters a lot, because that’s the margin where Goldman gets its edge over competitors that have access to the same AI models and platforms. ( Business Insider )

Figure 1: The Part 1 solution with AgentCore Gateway, Policy, and Observability, a second agent on Amazon EKS, and the audit path, with numbers matching the steps that follow The user signs in, and the backend for frontend (BFF) exchanges the ID token for an Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant (ID-JAG) issued to the task agent, agent A, as in Part 1.

In Part 1 , you built a task agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore , a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. The agent runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and acts for signed-in users through Okta Cross App Access (XAA). Okta decided which agent might act for which user, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, redeemed Okta’s grant inside the agent. That proves the governance mechanism, and it runs on a deliberately small topology: one agent, two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and the authorization check written into each server.
The mechanism scales. The topology doesn’t. Three things that are fine for one agent and two tools become the work in an enterprise with hundreds of agents and thousands of tools:

In this post, you make that change on the Part 1 solution. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, becomes the single front door and redeems Okta’s grant for each target. Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore evaluates Cedar policies that bind each tool to the agent and the scope Okta delegated. A second agent on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) joins under its own Okta identity, to show that the front door doesn’t care where an agent runs. And Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Observability, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, with Amazon CloudWatch gives you one place to read every decision, including Okta’s. We also compare XAA with per-user OAuth consent for applications that can’t accept Okta’s grant.

Over the past year, as we built Amazon Quick, our agents went from answering questions to taking actions: scheduling meetings, running research, generating reports. As the system evolved, one problem kept resurfacing: there was no shared definition of the primitives that agentic work is built from. The same few ideas kept getting rebuilt under different names: an actor that does the work, a signal that starts it, a packaged procedure, and a memory that carries lessons forward. This repetition leaked into product design and onto the user.

Take the user who says “ monitor my Slack channel and send me a daily digest ”. Is that a new agent, a scheduled instruction to an existing one, a workflow, or a skill? These are different questions, but without a shared vocabulary they collapse into one confusing choice.

This post shares the taxonomy we converged on: one set of primitives found by decomposing agentic work into four plain questions: When? , What? , Who? , and How? Most of the framework stays invisible to end users by design, but a shared vocabulary makes the system easier to reason about for anyone building beneath it.

articles.title: SageMaker Inference now supports Multi-Instance GPU to maximize GPU utilization for model endpoints | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: Amazon SageMaker Inference now supports GPU partitioning with NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), which divides one GPU into hardware-isolated partitions so you can run a different model in each or take a right-sized fraction of a newer accelerator. This post shows how two optional API fields place one model per partition, and what we measured against a whole older GPU.
articles.titleEn: SageMaker Inference now supports Multi-Instance GPU to maximize GPU utilization for model endpoints | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: Use multi-model endpoints – These load and unload models from a shared GPU on demand, which fits sparse, bursty traffic.
Today, Amazon SageMaker Inference supports GPU partitioning, which uses NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) to divide a physical GPU into independent partitions.

Because the split is in hardware rather than software, you get guarantees that other sharing methods can’t give: Predictable latency – Each partition has dedicated memory bandwidth, so one model’s traffic spike doesn’t show up in another model’s p99.

paragraphs: Use multi-model endpoints – These load and unload models from a shared GPU on demand, which fits sparse, bursty traffic.
Today, Amazon SageMaker Inference supports GPU partitioning, which uses NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) to divide a physical GPU into independent partitions.

When you deploy a model to a GPU endpoint, the smallest unit of GPU you can request is one whole accelerator.

This constraint can cost you twice. First, you can’t host more models on an instance than it has accelerators. An ml.p4d.24xlarge has eight A100s, so it holds eight models, whether each one needs 40 GB or 14 GB. Second, and less obvious, it makes every deployment come down to a choice of which full GPU to deploy to. As your concurrency and prompt lengths grow, a full GPU on an older instance stops being enough, but a full GPU on a newer one is more than your model can use. You end up either under-served or paying for capability you never reach.

Today, Amazon SageMaker Inference supports GPU partitioning, which uses NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) to divide a physical GPU into independent partitions. Each partition receives a fixed share of the GPU’s compute units and a dedicated block of its memory, with isolation enforced in hardware. That changes both constraints: you can place a different model in each partition, and you can choose a fraction of a newer accelerator instead of a whole one of either generation.

sourceContent.headline: OPPO Brings ColorOS 17 to the UAE: Silky Smooth. Flow with AI | OPPO UAE
sourceContent.description: OPPO's ColorOS 17 arrives in the UAE, debuting on the Find X10 Series with Living Flow Design, smoother performance and new AI features like AI Mind Pilot.
paragraphs: With the Laminar Flow Engine, app launch stability improves by 55%, while Gallery thumbnails load up to 50% faster on first launch compared with ColorOS 16.
1 ColorOS 17 expands OPPO AI with system-level agentic capabilities designed not only to answer questions, but also to help users complete complex tasks.
In tests simulating six years of use, ColorOS 17 retains over 90% of its initial smoothness, even with storage at 90% capacity.

Dubai, UAE, October 13 2026 –OPPO today unveiled ColorOS 17, the latest generation of its mobile operating system, delivering a new level of smoothness alongside more intelligent, system-level AI capabilities. Debuting on the upcoming Find X10 Series and rolling out progressively to more OPPO devices, ColorOS 17 will bring these new experiences to users worldwide.

From Parallel Animation in ColorOS 15 to Seamless Animation in ColorOS 16, smoothness has long been a defining quality of ColorOS. With ColorOS 17, OPPO takes this further, introducing the all-new Living Flow Design to make every interaction feel even more natural, continuous and responsive.

Living Flow Design is built around three core ideas: Luminous Effect, Fluid Motion and Flexible Feedback. Luminous Effect introduces softer, more translucent visuals, creating a refined sense of depth and hierarchy, while subtle lighting naturally guides attention and responds to touch. Fluid Motion enables interface elements to move, merge and transform seamlessly from one state to the next, with this sense of continuity carried throughout the system. Flexible Feedback brings the same sense of responsiveness to touch. Buttons, toolbars and other interactive elements visibly compress, stretch and rebound in response to taps, giving each interaction a more immediate and tactile feel rather than a mechanical response. Together, these elements create a more fluid and cohesive experience across the system, making everything from app transitions and Fluid Cloud to everyday interactions feel more immediate and intuitive.

sourceContent.description: Clutch, backed by Lightspeed and SignalFire, was last valued at $85 million, according to a source.
paragraphs: Other VC-backed companies that Palo Alto Networks has scooped up this year include NEA-backed Embrace, for $325 million ; Chronosphere, an observability platform backed by Greylock and Lux Capital, for $2.95 billion ; and Koi, a cyber startup backed by Battery and Team8, for $231 million , according to regulatory filings.
In September, Palo Alto Networks acquired Console, a two-year-old startup that uses AI agents to automate routine IT help desk tasks.

Palo Alto Networks is in talks to acquire Clutch Security , a startup that secures AI agents’ access to company systems, for $500 million in cash plus additional milestone-based payouts, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

Three-year-old Clutch was last valued at $85 million when it raised a $20 million Series A round in January 2025, led by Lightspeed and SignalFire, according to our source. The startup is currently approaching $10 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). That means the acquisition, if completed, would value Clutch at about 50 times its ARR, a standard way of pricing software companies.
Palo Alto Networks and Clutch Security did not respond to a request for comment. The Information was the first to report the acquisition discussions.

The startup Tau Robotics is sending humanoid robots to clean San Francisco homes. They still need lots of human guidance, but they’re learning.

I’m not the sort of person who typically pays for a house cleaner. I’m too frugal, and I kind of enjoy putting on a podcast and going to town on my tub with a Magic Eraser. But when I saw an X post about a new humanoid-robot cleaning service in San Francisco, I immediately signed up for the waitlist. I wanted my apartment to feel like The Jetsons , even if just for an hour.

I was also motivated by journalistic interest. In order to ensure an authentic experience, I didn’t tell Tau Robotics, the startup behind the X post, that I was a journalist—though I did use my real name, so it’s possible someone looked me up. Tau’s long-term goal is to make autonomous cleaning robots a reality, but they’re not quite there yet: For now, the robots are piloted remotely by humans, who watch what’s going on via cameras mounted in the robots’ heads and wrists. As the robots clean, they collect data that Tau will use to train up their more independent descendants. Every counter successfully wiped and T-shirt successfully folded will help the models that power the robots learn to do better on the next go-round.

As the robots clean, they collect data that Tau will use to train up their more independent descendants. Every counter successfully wiped and T-shirt successfully folded will help the models that power the robots learn to do better on the next go-round.

sourceLines: At the time I booked, Tau was offering $30 for an hourlong cleaning with a single robot; now the charge is $60 per weekly cleaning with two robots, or $100 for a one-time visit.
Because this data is so valuable to Tau, the company charges less for cleaning than one might expect for such a cutting-edge product.
But when I saw an X post about a new humanoid-robot cleaning service in San Francisco, I immediately signed up for the waitlist.

Anticipation that Democrats’ ‘blue wave’ will lead to tighter rules on AI and datacenters sends tech stock plunging. Plus a big eight-legged surprise for customs officials in Peru

Good morning. Stock markets around the world have fallen sharply as a rout in US tech stocks spread across the Atlantic after the Democrats’ midterms victory led to fears of a slowdown in the AI industry. A sell-off on Wall Street on Thursday was followed by sharp falls in Asian stock markets on Friday morning. The dip in investor sentiment has also reached London.

Susannah Streeter, the chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said: “The tech sell-off has intensified. Big worries are colliding – the build-out of datacenters looks set to slow, which risks shredding the spending spree underpinning the boom, right at the time that investors have become super nervous about returns on this massive investment.”

InfoQ Homepage News Yelp Combines Native and Server-Driven UI for its AI Assistant

Yelp has adopted a hybrid user interface architecture for its AI Assistant, combining native mobile controls with server-driven conversation rendering to support faster interface changes across platforms. The design uses Yelp’s CHAOS framework, short for Content Hosting Architecture with Optimization Strategies, to render conversation content while keeping navigation and message input native.

Yelp Assistant launched on iOS in 2024 to help users create project requests for local service professionals. It has since expanded to answer questions about businesses and support actions such as reservations, appointments, and food orders.

SHENZHEN, 13 October 2026–Global smart device brand OPPO today announced a collaboration with Manus, a leading AI agent platform, to bring next-generation agentic AI experiences to smartphones. By integrating Manus' agentic capabilities to OPPO AI Mind Pilot, the collaboration will help users turn complex, multi-step tasks into ready-to-use results—advancing OPPO's vision for Personalized Proactive Intelligence, where AI understands users and proactively helps them get things done.

"Agentic AI marks an important shift from answering questions to helping users get things done." said Kai Tang, President of Software Engineering at OPPO. "Together with Manus, we are bringing more proactive and capable experiences to AI Mind Pilot, enabling AI to better understand users' intentions, take actions and complete tasks. Our goal is to make personal AI a natural part of everyday life and work."

"Smartphones are central to people's daily lives and support many of the tasks they handle every day, making them a natural platform for personal AI agents," said Tao Zhang, Co-Founder & CPO of Manus. "By bringing together Manus' agentic capabilities and OPPO's system-level integration, we can make advanced AI agents more accessible and help users complete multi-step tasks through simple, natural interactions."

Screen Time, the iPhone feature most people know for limiting app use, has become the most direct way to block Apple Intelligence in iOS 27 . That’s because Apple removed the single switch that used to turn every AI feature off at once. The Settings section once called Apple Intelligence & Siri is now just Siri, centered on the new Siri AI , and the remaining AI tools are scattered across several menus. Screen Time’s restrictions can shut down Writing Tools and image creation together, and a few other features need their own toggles. Here’s the full map.

Individual features can still be disabled, but they’re scattered across several menus in Settings and Screen Time rather than consolidated in one place. Here’s the current map of what can be turned off and where to find each control.

sourceContent.description: Learn how to build a serverless Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate that gives AI agents secure, metadata-driven access to an enterprise data lake. Exposing a new dataset requires only a JSON file, with no per-dataset integration code.
paragraphs: The pipeline picks up metadata files, generates vector embeddings with Amazon Titan Text Embeddings, and indexes them into Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases.

Organizations building applications powered by artificial intelligence (AI) face a recurring challenge: giving large language model (LLM) agents access to enterprise data lakes without duplicating integration logic across every agent and application. Most teams begin by wiring agents directly to databases and APIs, with no shared gateway such as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server in between. Each new dataset demands custom code, and each agent reimplements its own access control. As the number of datasets or agents grows, permission enforcement drifts, and onboarding a new data source becomes a multi-day engineering effort.

Our team supports Amazon’s North America Sort Center (NASC) network, where planning teams rely on operational data to manage capacity, labor, and package flow. To give those teams conversational access to that data, we built a serverless Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate to address this problem for planning teams in NASC. The server acts as a centralized, agent-agnostic gateway between AI agents and our enterprise data lake. Exposing a new dataset requires only a JSON metadata file that the server discovers automatically on the next pipeline sync.

In this post, we describe the architecture, show how a metadata-driven approach removes the need for per-dataset integration code, and explain how the serverless infrastructure supports multiple agents and applications in a multi-tenant environment.

articles.titleEn: The AI ‘credit card’ is getting costlier as CoreWeave bond yield tops 16%
summaryLinesEn: Coreweave's five-year credit default swaps spiked above 1,289 basis points on Thursday, widening above their October peak, according to Deutsche Bank.
Moratoriums could impact 45% of planned capacity in the U.S. with a large amount of that in Texas, according to Goldman Sachs.
Goldman tallies five AI bond deals totaling $67 billion since October 29, pushing total hyperscaler debt issuance this year to $296 billion.

Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) is one of the fastest-growing AI chipmakers in the world, but it usually doesn't attract as much attention as Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA). Unlike Nvidia, which produces general-purpose GPUs for data centers, Broadcom produces customized AI accelerators (XPUs) for hyperscalers. When deployed at scale, Broadcom's XPUs can process AI inference tasks faster and more efficiently than Nvidia's stand-alone GPUs.

In fiscal 2025 (which ended last November), Broadcom's AI chip sales soared 65% to $20 billion, or 31% of its top line. In fiscal 2026, it expects its AI chip revenue to surge 186% year over year to $58 billion, or 55% of its projected revenue.

articles.title: Analyze your Stripe data directly with your agent
articles.descEn: You can now use natural language to create an investor slide deck highlighting where your business outperformed in the previous quarter, or build a custom dashboard to understand why your Stripe revenue changed.
articles.titleEn: Analyze your Stripe data directly with your agent
summaryLinesEn: If you want to better understand your subscriptions business, Stripe can route the agent to track monthly recurring revenue over time and attribute changes to upgrades, downgrades, churn, and anything else that is important for you to understand and take action on.

We introduced the ability for you to connect compatible agents such as Claude and Cursor to your Stripe analytics data via Stripe’s MCP or by using the Queries API and Reports API directly—now available for all Stripe users.
To make use of your Stripe data, an agent needs to know which tables to use, how Stripe defines the relevant metrics, and how to construct the analysis.

sourceContent.headline: Analyze your Stripe data directly with your agent
sourceContent.description: You can now use natural language to create an investor slide deck highlighting where your business outperformed in the previous quarter, or build a custom dashboard to understand why your Stripe revenue changed.
paragraphs: If you want to better understand your subscriptions business, Stripe can route the agent to track monthly recurring revenue over time and attribute changes to upgrades, downgrades, churn, and anything else that is important for you to understand and take action on.

We introduced the ability for you to connect compatible agents such as Claude and Cursor to your Stripe analytics data via Stripe’s MCP or by using the Queries API and Reports API directly—now available for all Stripe users.

As AI becomes a larger part of how teams work, users increasingly tell us they want to access and analyze their Stripe data directly with the agents they use every day.

Agents can now have structured access to your Stripe data to help you make faster, better business decisions. We introduced the ability for you to connect compatible agents such as Claude and Cursor to your Stripe analytics data via Stripe’s MCP or by using the Queries API and Reports API directly—now available for all Stripe users. With natural language prompts, you can do things like create an investor slide deck highlighting where your business outperformed in the previous quarter, or build a custom dashboard to understand why your Stripe revenue changed.
The Queries API is free for all Stripe users through January 31, 2027. After that, you’ll pay per credit of API usage, with no monthly subscription required. The Reports API will remain free.

localization.title: 에이전트와 직접 Stripe 데이터를 분석하세요
summaryLines: 구독 비즈니스를 더 잘 이해하려는 경우 Stripe는 에이전트를 라우팅하여 시간이 지남에 따라 매월 반복되는 수익을 추적하고 업그레이드, 다운그레이드, 이탈 및 이해하고 조치를 취하는 데 중요한 기타 사항에 대한 변경 사항을 지정할 수 있음
Claude 및 Cursor와 같은 호환 에이전트를 Stripe의 MCP를 통해 또는 Queries API 및 Reports API를 직접 사용하여 Stripe 분석 데이터에 연결할 수 있는 기능을 도입함 · 이제 모든 Stripe 사용자가 사용할 수 있음
Stripe 데이터를 활용하려면 상담원은 사용할 테이블, Stripe이 관련 측정항목을 정의하는 방법, 분석을 구성하는 방법을 알아야 함

summaryLinesEn: 米中主導の国際社会への不安が広がるなか、ある調査によると国際社会から寄せられる安心感が日本はカナダに次いで高いという結果がでた。
日本はこれを活かし、アジアの一員という地理的特性をテコに国際協調の旗振り役となることで経済成長を促すことができるのではないか。

sourceContent.headline: A Closer Look at Phonon TTS. Launching High-Quality On-Device Speech That Tops the Benchmarks.
sourceContent.description: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
paragraphs: How Phonon did on the Hugging Face Open TTS Leaderboard Two weeks ago, we opened up Phonon, our small text-to-speech model that runs on your own device.
It needs no server and no network, and what you type stays with you.
On intelligibility, Phonon ranks first in German and Spanish , and in the top three in every language we evaluated, next to models up to 100 times its size.
How Phonon did on the Hugging Face Open TTS Leaderboard
Two weeks ago, we opened up Phonon, our small text-to-speech model that runs on your own device. It needs no server and no network, and what you type stays with you.

Most voice AI lives in the cloud: every sentence makes a round trip to a server. Phonon runs on your own device instead. Your text stays there and the voice works without a network. We’ve also opened the weights. Phonon 31m is Apache 2.0, so you can use it for free, even in a commercial product. The other models are CC BY-NC, so they’re free for non-commercial projects. If you’re building something commercial with those, pricing is based on your number of users, not how much speech you generate.

sourceContent.headline: The agentic era needs a computing platform everywhere – Arm is building it
sourceContent.description: The Arm platform and ecosystem remain central to delivering the consistency, choice and breadth that the agentic world demands.
paragraphs: Arm provides that platform, combining industry-leading performance per watt with the flexibility to choose between IP, compute subsystems or silicon, all underpinned by an unmatched software ecosystem of more than 22 million developers.

AI infrastructure is increasingly moving to Arm, with adoption across every major hyperscaler and Arm-based rack-scale servers overtaking x86 as the dominant accelerated computing platform, according to IDC .
The industry needs a platform that can deliver the consistency developers need with the freedom to differentiate.

We’re moving from an era dominated by generative AI into an increasingly agentic world. This next era of computing won’t be built in one place – it will form increasingly connected parts of one computing continuum – at the edge, where intelligence is personal; in the physical world, where it takes action, and in the cloud, where it is created. This creates a system-level challenge – workloads are becoming more distributed; models and compute requirements are increasingly diverse; systems are becoming more heterogeneous and autonomous; and software environments vary.

The industry needs a platform that can deliver the consistency developers need with the freedom to differentiate. Arm provides that platform, combining industry-leading performance per watt with the flexibility to choose between IP, compute subsystems or silicon, all underpinned by an unmatched software ecosystem of more than 22 million developers. Today, we unveiled a series of updates that illustrate our continued momentum in delivering intelligence everywhere.

At the edge, AI is becoming more continuous, contextual and immersive, placing new demands on the entire mobile compute platform. These experiences aren’t defined by a single AI workload or processor – AI needs to run on the right compute engine for the task. Our new Arm CSS for Mobile 2 platform is designed for that shift, delivering an AI-native compute foundation powered by two new best-in-class compute engines built for the AI era. The Arm C2 Ultra CPU with SME2 brings a new level of responsive, efficient on-device AI to the CPU, while the Arm Mali G2-Ultra NX GPU introduces dedicated neural accelerators that enable neural graphics to run natively on the GPU.

articles.title: The Long-Term Benefit Trust
articles.descEn: An independent body of five trustees with authority to elect and remove Anthropic board members, balancing stockholder and public interests.
articles.titleEn: The Long-Term Benefit Trust
summaryLinesEn: At the close of our Series C , we amended our corporate charter to create a new class of stock (Class T) held exclusively by the Trust.1 The Class T stock grants the Trust the authority to elect and remove a number of Anthropic’s board members that will phase in according to time- and funding-based milestones; in any event, the Trust will elect a majority of the board within 4 years.

For example, the LTBT can ensure that the organizational leadership is incentivized to carefully evaluate future models for catastrophic risks or ensure they have nation-state level security, rather than prioritizing being the first to market above all other objectives.
Paired with our Public Benefit Corporation status, the LTBT helps to align our corporate governance with our mission of developing and maintaining advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.

Announcements Oct 21, 2026 Physicist Christopher Stubbs joins Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust

Today we are sharing more details about our new governance structure called the Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT) , which we have been developing since the birth of Anthropic. The LTBT is our attempt to fine-tune our corporate governance to address the unique challenges and long-term opportunities we believe transformative AI will present .

The Trust is an independent body of five financially disinterested members with an authority to select and remove a portion of our Board that will grow over time (ultimately, a majority of our Board). Paired with our Public Benefit Corporation status, the LTBT helps to align our corporate governance with our mission of developing and maintaining advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.

articles.title: Hot Chips 2026: The CPU’s next chapter is being built on Arm
articles.descEn: Hot Chips 2026 showed how IBM, Fujitsu, NVIDIA and Arm are redefining the CPU for agentic AI around a common Arm software foundation.
articles.titleEn: Hot Chips 2026: The CPU’s next chapter is being built on Arm
summaryLinesEn: But the CPU sessions at Hot Chips revealed something else.: Arm showed up almost everywhere.
The designs could hardly be more different, spanning mission-critical enterprise computing, green data centers, accelerated AI systems and purpose-built agentic infrastructure.
The resulting design integrates up to 136 Arm Neoverse V3 cores, 12 DDR5 memory channels, 96 lanes of PCIe Gen6 and CXL 3.0 support within a 300-watt TDP.
articles.summary:

sourceContent.headline: Hot Chips 2026: The CPU’s next chapter is being built on Arm
sourceContent.description: Hot Chips 2026 showed how IBM, Fujitsu, NVIDIA and Arm are redefining the CPU for agentic AI around a common Arm software foundation.
paragraphs: But the CPU sessions at Hot Chips revealed something else.: Arm showed up almost everywhere.
The designs could hardly be more different, spanning mission-critical enterprise computing, green data centers, accelerated AI systems and purpose-built agentic infrastructure.
The resulting design integrates up to 136 Arm Neoverse V3 cores, 12 DDR5 memory channels, 96 lanes of PCIe Gen6 and CXL 3.0 support within a 300-watt TDP.
Hot Chips 2026 made two things clear: agentic AI is creating a new CPU moment and the industry’s next generation of CPUs is increasingly being built on Arm.

As AI moves from answering questions to reasoning, planning, retrieving data, invoking tools and taking action, more of the work around the model falls to the CPU. Agentic systems need to run code, coordinate services, move data, manage memory and storage and keep increasingly specialized accelerators supplied with useful work.

paragraphs: Cobalt 200 was optimized for EDA workloads through increased cache size and improved memory bandwidth per core.

Designing Azure silicon on Azure silicon: EDA workloads on Cobalt 200

Every Azure chip Microsoft has built started as electronic design automation (EDA) jobs used to design, test, and validate silicon before it is manufactured. This includes simulation sweeps that run for days, verification regressions that fan out across thousands of cores overnight, and physical signoff runs that use hundreds of gigabytes of memory for a single block. Together, these workloads account for hundreds of millions of compute jobs each year. Today we’re sharing early results from our next step in that evolution: running EDA workloads on Azure Cobalt 200 , Azure’s custom compute infrastructure built on the Arm Neoverse CSS V3. In our silicon design environment, the evaluated EDA workloads ran with 1.30x to 4.15x more performance than on Cobalt 100 across a range of testing scenarios, from simulation to verification to static timing analysis.

Traditionally, EDA workloads ran on fixed, on-premise x86 server capacity, sized for peak demand with periods of underutilization. The shift to cloud-based EDA on Microsoft Azure offered a new level of flexibility, scale, and reliability on compute-intensive silicon design workloads. Using Azure Cobalt-based virtual machine (VM) instances, silicon engineering teams at Microsoft are experiencing significant performance and efficiency improvements on EDA workloads that Azure customers are seeing across many workloads—optimizing the performance and speed of designing increasingly sophisticated silicon for increasingly complex cloud systems.

articles.title: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge
articles.descEn: NVIDIA intentionally designs GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software together to get more useful work out of memory at every layer of the AI factory.
articles.titleEn: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge
summaryLinesEn: At 125 tokens per second per user, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers up to 30x higher throughput per dollar than GB300 NVL72, with HBM capacity per GPU up about 3%.
NVIDIA was first to adopt HBM3e and HBM4 technologies into an accelerated computing stack.

Recent models, including FLUX.2 [klein] from Black Forest Labs , Inkling from Thinking Machines Lab, Beam 1.0 from Reflection , Meta Muse Spark from Meta , Step 5 Preview from StepFun and NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL have been released with NVFP4 checkpoints, demonstrating growing model-builder adoption of 4-bit precision for faster, more memory-efficient inference.

articles.title: Scaling trust in confidential AI requires a common language
articles.descEn: Arm and Fujitsu explore how CoServe, IETF RATS and Veraison can help standardize attestation across increasingly heterogeneous confidential AI systems.
articles.titleEn: Scaling trust in confidential AI requires a common language
summaryLinesEn: And for the wider ecosystem, it provides something equally important: a common language through which different parts of an increasingly diverse computing supply chain can participate in trust.
These factors create a scaling problem the industry needs to address.

CoSERV is an adopted work item within the IETF RATS working group designed to provide a common conveyance mechanism through which verifiers can obtain endorsements and reference values from potentially complex supply-chain sources.

sourceContent.headline: Scaling trust in confidential AI requires a common language
sourceContent.description: Arm and Fujitsu explore how CoServe, IETF RATS and Veraison can help standardize attestation across increasingly heterogeneous confidential AI systems.
paragraphs: And for the wider ecosystem, it provides something equally important: a common language through which different parts of an increasingly diverse computing supply chain can participate in trust.
These factors create a scaling problem the industry needs to address.

CoSERV is an adopted work item within the IETF RATS working group designed to provide a common conveyance mechanism through which verifiers can obtain endorsements and reference values from potentially complex supply-chain sources.
Confidential computing changes an important assumption about how trust works in modern infrastructure.

Traditionally, attestation has largely been an internal concern for infrastructure providers. Within a data center, operators can use attestation to check the integrity of servers and determine whether services should be allowed to run or connect to other resources. These trust decisions are important, but they generally remain inside the boundaries of the infrastructure being managed.

AI systems increasingly bring together CPUs, GPUs and other accelerators, firmware, software and services from multiple suppliers. At the same time, more parties have a stake in whether those systems can be trusted. Model providers want assurance that valuable models will run only in appropriately protected environments. Users want confidence that their data remains protected while it is being processed. And infrastructure providers still need to verify the integrity of the underlying platform.
