articles.title: The Wizard of Open Weights: Chris Alexiuk Makes AI Easy With Open Models
articles.descEn: Chris Alexiuk is a senior product research engineer in deep learning at NVIDIA who specializes in making open large language models (LLMs) practical for working developers.
articles.titleEn: The Wizard of Open Weights: Chris Alexiuk Makes AI Easy With Open Models
summaryLinesEn: “I think Nemotron is the most important project that exists,” said Alexiuk, who also uses the pseudonym “Joe Nemotron” across social media.
“It would be the greatest day of my life to be surpassed by an even bigger fan of Nemotron, who had heard about Nemotron through the work I was doing,” Alexiuk said.

“There’s a category of model that’s going to be close to the kind of work you want to accomplish,” Alexiuk said, explaining that Nemotron supports that whole ecosystem of AI users: from individual developers using a model like Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for repetitive, high-frequency execution work to a company deploying Nemotron Ultra for long-running autonomous agents, deep research and enterprise tasks.

Chris Alexiuk has a simple rule about open source AI: If you believe in it, be loud about it.

“We should be shouting about this technology from the rooftops,” said Alexiuk, a Toronto-based senior product research engineer in deep learning at NVIDIA who specializes in making open large language models (LLMs) practical for working developers.

Alexiuk는 "당신이 달성하고자 하는 작업 종류에 가까운 모델 범주가 있습니다"라고 Nemotron은 반복적이고 빈도가 높은 실행 작업을 위해 Nemotron 3.5 Lightning과 같은 모델을 사용하는 개인 개발자부터 장기 실행 자율 에이전트, 심층 연구 및 기업 작업을 위해 Nemotron Ultra를 배포하는 회사에 이르기까지 AI 사용자의 전체 생태계를 지원한다고 설명함

articles.title: From Delta Sharing to OpenSharing: what changed, what's next | Databricks Blog
articles.descEn: Delta Sharing is now OpenSharing: an open protocol for sharing tables, agent skills, AI models, and unstructured data across platforms.
articles.titleEn: From Delta Sharing to OpenSharing: what changed, what's next | Databricks Blog
summaryLinesEn: By the time Databricks announced OpenSharing in June 2026, Delta Sharing had reached more than 28,000 data recipients, with roughly a third of shares flowing across platforms through open connectors rather than staying inside Databricks-to-Databricks sharing ( Databricks blog ).

When Databricks introduced Delta Sharing at Data + AI Summit 2021, the core problem it addressed was simple to state and hard to solve well: organizations wanted to share live data with partners, customers, and other teams, without exporting files, standing up brittle ETL jobs, or forcing every recipient onto the same platform.
Existing Delta Sharing setups keep working, and you enable the new asset types on a Unity Catalog metastore using the same share, recipient, and grant workflow.

localization.title: Delta Sharing에서 OpenSharing으로 · 변경된 사항과 다음 단계 | 데이터브릭스 블로그
summaryLines: Databricks가 2026년 6월 OpenSharing을 발표할 때까지 Delta Sharing은 28,000명이 넘는 데이터 수신자에게 도달했으며, 공유의 약 3분의 1은 Databricks-Databricks 공유 내부에 머물지 않고 개방형 커넥터를 통해 플랫폼 간에 이동했습니다(Databricks 블로그)
Databricks가 Data + AI Summit 2021에서 델타 공유를 도입했을 때 해결한 핵심 문제는 설명하기는 간단하지만 잘 해결하기는 어렵음 · 조직은 파일을 내보내거나 취약한 ETL 작업을 수행하거나 모든 수신자를 동일한 플랫폼에 강제로 적용하지 않고 파트너, 고객 및 다른 팀과 실시간 데이터를 공유하기를 원함
기존 델타 공유 설정은 계속 작동하며 동일한 공유, 수신자 및 권한 부여 워크플로를 사용하여 Unity 카탈로그 메타스토어에서 새로운 자산 유형을 활성화함

articles.title: Stop treating agents as one-off projects and start running them as a continuous discipline | Microsoft Azure Blog
articles.descEn: Learn why Microsoft Foundry is the enterprise AI platform to build, ground, and govern AI apps and agents at scale.
articles.titleEn: Stop treating agents as one-off projects and start running them as a continuous discipline | Microsoft Azure Blog
summaryLinesEn: Stop treating agents as one-off projects and start running them as a continuous discipline Transformation begins at the line between an experiment that works and a capability the business depends on.

A new IDC InfoBrief, sponsored by Microsoft, Scaling AI Without Scaling Costs *, on how organizations are funding and governing AI, shows both the urgency of that shift and the friction holding it back.

Only 17% of organizations build models to project how costs scale in production—even as about 78% prioritize cost efficiency when selecting a model. 86% expect financial results within six to 24 months—roughly one budget cycle to show something real.

Transformation begins at the line between an experiment that works and a capability the business depends on. Scaling intelligence requires production capabilities built for sustained business performance, with investments prioritized against financial thresholds, tied to measurable outcomes, instrumented for unit costs, and owned by accountable leaders. This approach manages cost, performance, governance, and reliability as adoption grows.

paragraphs: Selling partners using high-quality A+ Content boost their sales by 8–20 percent compared to those without it.

The baseline reached 0.80 accuracy and an F1 score of 0.84 on the high-quality class.

A+ Content is the rich media widget on the Amazon product detail page. Through visual assets, brands communicate unique product and brand value to help customers make informed purchase decisions. Selling partners using high-quality A+ Content boost their sales by 8–20 percent compared to those without it. A wide variety of brands, from established brands with large in-house design teams to bootstrapped brands with limited resources, use A+ Content, creating inconsistency in content quality. A typical A+ Content project combines text, images, and video into a cohesive product story. Evaluating each asset in isolation misses the quality that emerges from how those assets work together. When your content spans multiple heterogeneous modules and you need a holistic quality signal rather than per-asset checks, the multi-model fusion approach described in this post can help. In this post, we examine this problem in the context of A+ Content.

A+ Content provides creative freedom for selling partners to express their authentic selves on their product detail pages, without strict content specifications such as image ratio and text word count.
Although this flexibility allows compelling brand storytelling, it also creates substantial variation in content composition and quality.

summaryLinesEn: Why it matters: NVIDIA Vera delivers both fast agent performance and high capacity per watt within a single CPU.

sourceContent.description: Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore returns a synthesized, source-cited answer to a natural-language question in a single tool call, with no search, retrieve, synthesize, and citation pipeline to build. Learn how it works and how to add it to an AgentCore Gateway and call it from an agent.
paragraphs: Web Answer runs new searches for every question, and its model is given today’s date so it can search for up-to-date information.

Figure 1: Request flow from an agent through the Gateway to Web Answer and back Your agent sends a question to your AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

Today, we are announcing the general availability of Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. With Web Answer, agent builders get a synthesized, source-cited answer to a natural-language question with a single tool call. They no longer build a search, retrieve, synthesize, and citation pipeline themselves.

If you have built agents that need to answer questions from current web sources, you know the pattern: call a search API, decide which results to trust, retrieve and clean page content, prompt a model to synthesize, and engineer citation extraction so the output traces back to a source. Every step is code you maintain, and every step is another place things can go wrong: hallucination when evidence is insufficient, stale content when the index moves, and broken attribution when a claim and its source drift apart.

The Web Answer collapses that entire pipeline into one request. You send a question. You get back a cited answer in seconds. In this post, we explain what Web Answer does, compare it with Web Search on AgentCore, show how it works and what it returns, and walk through adding Web Answer to a gateway and calling it from an agent.

We built Anon to help enterprise AI agents securely use websites the way people do. That means navigating pages and taking actions like signing in or filling out forms, even when there’s no API. We’re excited to share that Anon is joining Sierra, bringing our team’s expertise and access to our technology to agents that already handle billions of customer interactions each year.

Before Anon, I co-founded Spring Labs and spent years working on identity and data security for financial services companies. As AI agents started to emerge in early 2023, I saw a problem that felt familiar. If agents were going to act for people, they’d need a secure way to sign in and take action as them.

AI is commoditizing the basic building blocks of many customer experiences. Across industries, those building blocks are high-volume workflows, like order tracking and returns in retail, appointment scheduling in healthcare, first notice of loss and document collection in insurance, and ID verification and dispute intake in lending.

Accelerators create and maintain these workflows out-of-the-box along with basic integrations and guardrails, while Ghostwriter customizes them for your business. summaryLinesEn: Established in 2011, the Hall of Innovation recognizes privately held technology companies that have made a significant impact at JPMorganChase through their innovation, business value, and close collaboration with the firm’s teams.
Sierra, the leading customer experience AI platform, today announced its induction into JPMorganChase’s Hall of Innovation.

“Agentic AI has the potential to create simpler, more intuitive experiences for customers, but realizing that potential requires getting trust, security and controls right from the start,” said Gill Haus, Chief Information Officer of Chase.

articles.title: BofA lifts Supermicro target despite AI margin concerns
articles.descEn: Record sales and strong AI demand prompted higher forecasts, but BofA remains concerned about profit margins and cash flow.
articles.titleEn: BofA lifts Supermicro target despite AI margin concerns
summaryLinesEn: Bank of America raised its Supermicro price target to $39 from $38 after the AI server maker reported record quarterly revenue, but maintained its Underperform rating over concerns about future profit margins and cash flow.

Also read: Warren Buffett shares a simple rule for surviving a market crash The company's reported margins and full-year outlook show the difference: During the company's Nov. 3 earnings call , Chief Financial Officer Mark Long said the sequential decline largely reflected a shift toward large AI data-center projects, which generally carry lower margins than the company's enterprise and channel business.
Long also said during the earnings call that the company expects a gross margin of 12% to 12.5% for the quarter.

summaryLinesEn: Qualcomm and Nvidia both dropped more than 9%, with the latter losing almost $450 billion in market cap.
Intel last week reported a 78% jump in data center revenue, but the stock got crushed due to a weaker-than-expected forecast from the memory shortage.

Chipmakers plummeted on Thursday, with Nvidia pushing the Nasdaq to its worst day in 19 months, after this week's midterm election results raised concerns on Wall Street that the artificial intelligence buildout is poised to slow down.

paragraphs: To further advance the pace of research, we’re offering 10,000 scientists the highest usage tier in Google Antigravity free of charge for 6 months (onboarded on a rolling basis), subject to eligibility, capacity, and selection.
Accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity

LeVine Designing new medicines requires curating complex data from charts, figures and literature, training predictive models, and proposing candidate molecules to synthesize — a workflow that typically takes multiple days for a single iteration.
Zoi Tsangalidou, Ruijie (Kelly) Zhang, Sukhdeep Singh and Michael V. LeVine

Designing new medicines requires curating complex data from charts, figures and literature, training predictive models, and proposing candidate molecules to synthesize — a workflow that typically takes multiple days for a single iteration.

Here we show how Google Antigravity , equipped with our new Cheminformatics Skills, accelerates drug discovery workflows. Using real-world lung cancer treatments, an agent searches through thousands of compounds, performs matched molecular pair analysis, and proposes novel rigidified macrocycles with synthetic routes in just an hour.

ROBLOX claimed the top spot as the world’s highest-grossing mobile game in October 2026. Honor of Kings, Gossip Harbor, Royal Match and Whiteout Survival rounded out the global top five.

According to Sensor Tower’s App Performance Insights, ROBLOX ranked No. 1 worldwide in both revenue and revenue growth in October. Its Halloween campaign, The Hollow , connected nine horror experiences in a shared survival event. Each night, players explored a new maze and faced a monster from one of the participating games, including 99 Nights in the Forest , Animal Hospital , and Scary Shawarma Kiosk . Quests across the hub and participating games offered ways to explore Roblox’s horror lineup and earn avatar rewards, while limited-time Halloween items created opportunities for further engagement and spending.

Honor of Kings ranked No. 2 worldwide by revenue in October 2026. Its eight-day Anniversary Celebration began on October 24, with login rewards including tickets for an in-game prize draw and Rose Hearts—a currency used to redeem rare skins—and other anniversary items. The celebration also opened redemption for a limited-edition Legendary outfit, giving players a chance to claim a major cosmetic reward.

articles.descEn: Discover how Arm Performix Dynamic Insights combines runtime performance data with AI-powered analysis to help developers and coding agents identify bottlenecks, validate optimizations, and improve software performance on Arm-based platforms.

paragraphs: Developers can then ask follow-up questions, request additional explanations or challenge recommendations, while retaining access to the underlying performance evidence.

Agentic development and AI coding agents are changing software development by accelerating the generation, modification and refactoring of code. As these tools help developers move from idea to implementation faster, one challenge looms large: ensuring that the resulting code performs efficiently on the systems where it runs.

Generating functional code is only part of the engineering work. Developers still need to understand how applications behave under real workloads, where execution time is spent, how system resources are used, and which constraints limit performance. As AI produces more code at greater speed, this visibility is essential in preventing performance analysis from becoming a bottleneck.

Dynamic Insights , part of the latest release of Arm Performix , helps address this challenge. It enables developers and AI coding agents to turn detailed runtime data into evidence-based recommendations for optimizing software on Arm-based platforms.

paragraphs: More than 100,000 pull requests in our codebase later, my co-founder Fabian and our team of engineers, designers, and product managers have turned that plan into Lovable, and our users have created more than 70 million projects on the platform to date.
Improvements to that common setup could help across many projects.
Later that year I wrote down the plan for Lovable : people who couldn’t code would create, deploy, and improve software through chat and instantly see the result.

Making Lovable simple and dependable has meant repeatedly rethinking how it works. As the technical landscape keeps changing, engineering choices that once helped can start holding you back. Many teams building AI-powered products face the same question: what should you keep, and what should you rebuild?

In the spring of 2023, I put an open-source project called GPT Engineer on GitHub. You described the software you wanted, it asked clarifying questions, and then it wrote the whole codebase. Later that year I wrote down the plan for Lovable : people who couldn’t code would create, deploy, and improve software through chat and instantly see the result. More than 100,000 pull requests in our codebase later, my co-founder Fabian and our team of engineers, designers, and product managers have turned that plan into Lovable, and our users have created more than 70 million projects on the platform to date.

I recently reread my original plan, and it's eerily similar to what we ended up building. What I didn’t anticipate was how many times we would reinvent the way we get there. Along the way, we had to rethink how much freedom to give a model, how to catch its mistakes quickly, and even how to fork the computer it was working on.

sourceContent.headline: We're sharing our framework for building safer and more helpful AI for health.
paragraphs: The adoption of technology for health is accelerating and impacts billions of people every day.

By sharing our methodology, we hope to promote transparency in how we approach this important area, and seek to support the entire health ecosystem — from developers to researchers to clinicians — in building AI tools people can trust.
Dana Gelb Safran , we published a whitepaper detailing an end-to-end evaluation approach to assess AI use cases for addressing people’s health needs.

Many of us have turned to AI with a health question or received care from a doctor who’s using it. The adoption of technology for health is accelerating and impacts billions of people every day. But how can we assess if these tools are safe and helpful?

In partnership with health experts Dr. Elizabeth McGlynn and Dr. Dana Gelb Safran , we published a whitepaper detailing an end-to-end evaluation approach to assess AI use cases for addressing people’s health needs. The framework evaluates models across three areas: accuracy, safety, and usefulness. It combines closed-question benchmarks, autoraters, and expert human review to assess common and high-risk health scenarios.

We built and continue to utilize this framework to assess whether our models provide useful, accurate responses that promote safe interactions in health contexts. By sharing our methodology, we hope to promote transparency in how we approach this important area, and seek to support the entire health ecosystem — from developers to researchers to clinicians — in building AI tools people can trust.

Predicting and detecting failures: How Azure strengthens reliability for mission-critical workloads

Takeaway : Azure Failure Prediction and Detection (AFPD) is Microsoft Azure’s end-to-end system aiming to catch hardware failures before they interrupt a workload, not after. Across the Azure fleet, AFPD has improved the prevention of hardware-related VM interruptions by 36% . SAP workloads offer a compelling example of AFPD’s value, illustrating why preventing interruptions matters for mission-critical services. But AFPD isn’t specific to SAP: it operates across General Purpose, Specialized Compute, HPC/AI, and select Storage workloads, making SAP’s experience a window into Azure’s broader approach to reliability for mission-critical third-party services. To learn more, watch our companion video to learn how AFPD helps reduce the risk of failures disrupting your critical workloads.

Most conversations about cloud reliability focus on what you build: zone-redundant architectures, failover patterns, and backup strategies. Less visible, but just as consequential, is what the platform does on your behalf; before a failure ever becomes an incident you need to respond to.

articles.title: How U Mobile built agentic telco operations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: U Mobile, Malaysia's newest 5G network provider, built AiDaH, an agentic AI operations platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that moves beyond AI assistance to autonomous action across telco operations. Nine months after production launch, AiDaH handles over 150 operational scenarios across six divisions, cutting trouble tickets by up to 84.5%.
articles.titleEn: How U Mobile built agentic telco operations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: U Mobile’s internal measurements show trouble ticket volumes falling by up to 84.5 percent in key categories.
Through 2026 the platform hardened and expanded, adding three-tier routing and reaching 6 agents by mid-year.

Roughly 70 percent of requests resolve through deterministic keyword matching with no model invocation, 20 percent are classified by a lightweight model, and only 10 percent require the full orchestrator.

paragraphs: U Mobile’s internal measurements show trouble ticket volumes falling by up to 84.5 percent in key categories.
Through 2026 the platform hardened and expanded, adding three-tier routing and reaching 6 agents by mid-year.

Roughly 70 percent of requests resolve through deterministic keyword matching with no model invocation, 20 percent are classified by a lightweight model, and only 10 percent require the full orchestrator.

U Mobile, Malaysia’s newest 5G network provider, has always run its telco operations lean, doing more with less through continuous automation. When new AI capabilities became available, U Mobile explored how to enhance operational efficiency beyond basic productivity gains. The real opportunity was further upstream, in how operations teams diagnose and resolve problems in the first place. The same lean operating discipline shaped the foundation for AiDaH: not a one-off technology initiative, but the next step in a long-running journey to simplify operations and scale capability without adding complexity.

When a subscriber can’t purchase a data add-on, resolving it isn’t a single problem. It’s a coordination problem. A customer service agent needs to pull interface logs for error codes. The same agent must then query business support system APIs for subscriber eligibility, and cross-reference internal knowledge bases for applicable business policies. All of that happens across multiple systems, before drafting a single word of response. And when that fails, the ticket escalates to backend IT teams and the subscriber waits even longer.

Traditional automation tools can help agents write better responses. What they can’t do is navigate multiple systems, analyze the results, and propose corrective action. Closing that gap takes an agentic architecture built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

This post is co-written with Shravan K S from Indegene Limited.

Enterprise AI is creating new opportunities for life sciences organizations to improve decision-making across commercial, medical, market access, and other business functions. But the quality of every AI model, dashboard, and business insight depends on one thing: trusted data. As enterprise data grows across multiple platforms, pipelines, and business domains, maintaining consistent data quality has become increasingly difficult. Manual data quality rule creation, fragmented governance, and evolving business definitions make it challenging to scale data quality across the enterprise.

This post explores how Indegene built a production-grade, large language model (LLM) powered Data Quality Agent within its NEXT Unified Data Platform (NEXT UDP) on AWS. The agent generates context-aware data quality rules, validates them, and produces ready-to-run SQL and Python code under centralized, human-in-the-loop governance. Together, these capabilities help organizations improve data quality at enterprise scale while reducing the effort required to build and maintain data quality programs.

sourceContent.description: In production AI agents, context management is the real bottleneck. This post presents a four-layer context engineering framework (architecture, prompts, file-based tools, and verification agents), implemented in working code from Deep Insight, an open source multi-agent data analysis solution on the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
paragraphs: In Deep Insight, all agents share one standardized format: Implementation detail 2-2: Self-contained code philosophy The Coder agent’s prompt explicitly states “variables do not persist between scripts.”
It introduced how Strands Agents SDK , Amazon Bedrock and Bedrock AgentCore , and AWS Fargate each address different layers of the problem, with code examples.

The prompt provides both incorrect and correct examples: The reason this rule relates to context engineering is that referencing variables from previous scripts requires the agent to “remember” prior conversations, which means past code must remain in context.

When production AI agents handle tasks such as data analysis and report generation, context management can become a major bottleneck. A 200K-token window sounds generous until a real-world task burns through most of it in minutes. Data analysis and report generation leave the agent failing mid-execution, losing accuracy, or driving up costs. A body of published guidance already addresses this, but the individual techniques are easier to read about than to apply. Applied together, they make a measurable difference: in the reference implementation this post walks through, a single write-and-execute tool cuts the tokens each script adds to context by about 95 percent, and loading skills on demand shrinks the system prompt by about 97 percent.

This series organizes that guidance into practices you can apply directly. Anthropic’s engineering posts, together with features built into the Strands Agents SDK, converge on four layers of context engineering: isolate context at the architecture level, control it through prompts, externalize it to the filesystem, and verify it with independent agents and safeguards. In this post (Part 2), you will learn how each layer works and what it looks like in working code. We applied these techniques in Deep Insight , an open source multi-agent data analysis solution built on the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, which serves as the reference implementation throughout.
Part 1: 5 production challenges in multi-agent systems and how Deep Insight solved them.

sourceContent.headline: Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick: Human oversight where it matters | Amazon Web Services
sourceContent.description: Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick reviews eligible agent actions within your existing controls, reducing unnecessary approval prompts while keeping consequential decisions with a person. See how policy sets the boundary, how a classifier reviews actions, and how AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch Logs support audit.
paragraphs: That would change the audience beyond the recipients she specified, so Smart Approvals is designed to return the proposed send to her for review, where she can decline it.
With Smart Approvals enabled, an action is eligible only when the user’s setting is “Ask each time” and no other control requires human approval.
Research on security warnings shows that attention and adherence can decline with repetition.

How should security leaders preserve human oversight as AI agents take on more work? Permissions establish which actions agents can take, but a permitted action can still warrant a person’s judgment. Requiring approval for every step might seem like the safest approach, yet multi-step tasks can produce repeated prompts , even for routine actions. Research on security warnings shows that attention and adherence can decline with repetition. The challenge isn’t to require more approvals, but to preserve attention for decisions that need human review.

Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick addresses this challenge by reviewing eligible actions within your existing controls. It evaluates each proposed action against the user’s request and either approves it automatically or returns it to the user for review. It does this without granting additional permissions or removing required human approvals. Security leaders retain control over which actions must always go to a person, while Smart Approvals is designed to reduce unnecessary interruptions in routine work.
Figure 1: Policy determines eligibility. Smart Approvals approves eligible actions or returns them to the user for review. Policy denials remain blocked

A MIDI file holds the exact notes and timing of a musical part, so it gives you a much more precise starting point than any other way of creating on Suno. You can decide how closely Suno follows it, for example, ask the model to play your notes exactly as you wrote them, or it can take a motif from the file and develop it into something new.

One of the most enjoyable parts of making music on Suno is taking one idea and turning it into something completely different. A text prompt, whether it’s simple or detailed, can become an entirely new sonic world. When you upload or drag and drop your own audio onto the Create page, Suno expands on your idea while keeping the sound that makes it yours. MIDI is the newest of these starting points, and it works differently from the other uploadable assets because a MIDI file contains no sound at all. To see why that’s useful, it helps to know what MIDI actually is.

In April, we released DharmaOCR-LITE , a model specialized for OCR across a wide range of documents, from contracts and court filings to invoices, IDs and forms. paragraphs: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, scores an agent through its entire lifecycle, on demand during development, in batch jobs against stored sessions, and online against production traffic.
This code sample helps you set up the framework for testing decision models compared to LLM-as-a-judge for your own use cases.

Figure 3: How the code-based evaluator Lambda adapts OpenTelemetry spans for the decision model and maps the result back to AgentCore The adapter converts the model’s probability distribution into a result that AgentCore evaluation expects.

Some of the questions you ask when evaluating an agent are narrow and repeatable. Did this response stay on policy? Is this tool call safe to approve? Does this answer match the retrieved context? Decision models answer exactly that kind of question. They take a structured state and a fixed set of allowed answers and return a calibrated probability over them, rather than free-form text whose confidence drifts from run to run. That makes them a strong fit for the scoring step in an agent evaluation, where you want a label and a number you can threshold and trust.

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, scores an agent through its entire lifecycle, on demand during development, in batch jobs against stored sessions, and online against production traffic. Alongside 15 built-in evaluators, AgentCore Evaluations supports custom evaluators that you define as either an LLM-as-a-judge or a code-based evaluator. Custom LLM-as-a-judge evaluators apply your instructions and rating scale with a model in Amazon Bedrock. Code-based evaluators run your own logic in an AWS Lambda function, and that logic can call your choice of external system, model, or API, including a decision model.

Decision models suit questions with a fixed set of answers that an informed person could decide at a glance, such as whether the agent refused a request or whether a response stayed on topic. After you validate a question on your own traffic, a decision model can be sufficient for that decision or score, and you can extend the same approach to specific harmfulness or stereotyping categories in your policy. Because both backends can answer several questions about the same state in a single request, you can use them as a screening layer rather than a replacement, running a pass or fail signal across your metrics to select the turns that warrant deeper assessment by the built-in evaluators, whose explanations help you investigate what went wrong.

paragraphs: The AI voice startup has deployed an inbound sales development representative (SDR) agent that has handled over 3,000 customer leads this year, qualifying over 90% of those potential clients in 32 different languages without any human intervention.

Marvell says the deal will allow the combined company to address a market worth $550 billion, with Chairman and CEO Matt Murphy saying, “AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation.”
He says that the efficiency gains ElevenLabs reaps from agentic AI may feel cutting edge today, but “in six months time, you can see even more gains.”
Alex Holt, the field chief technology officer at ElevenLabs, is about as bullish on AI agents as a C-suite leader can get.

The AI voice startup has deployed an inbound sales development representative (SDR) agent that has handled over 3,000 customer leads this year, qualifying over 90% of those potential clients in 32 different languages without any human intervention. Yet another AI agent serves as a coach to help new sales team members role-play customers interactions, resulting in faster onboarding for that part of the workforce. There’s also a recruiting agent that conducts first-round interviews with new job candidates, and within the company’s Slack, various agents are quick to jump in and answer any employee questions about internal processes.

“I think what’s most exciting about this space is that you know you always feel like you’re on the tip of the iceberg,” says Holt. He says that the efficiency gains ElevenLabs reaps from agentic AI may feel cutting edge today, but “in six months time, you can see even more gains.”

그는 에이전트 AI를 통해 ElevenLabs가 얻는 효율성이 오늘날 최첨단이라고 느낄 수 있지만 "6개월 후에는 훨씬 더 많은 이점을 얻을 수 있습니다"라고 말함

summaryLinesEn: In our continued pursuit to push the horizon at Collinear AI , CWE-bench v2 opens up a public set of 100 tasks that anyone can run and evaluate their models on.

On cost, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1017), Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon form the Pareto frontier: DeepSeek reaches 57.0% pass@1 at $0.04 per rollout, Opus adds ten points at $1.83, and Gemini edges ahead at $3.92.

paragraphs: In our continued pursuit to push the horizon at Collinear AI , CWE-bench v2 opens up a public set of 100 tasks that anyone can run and evaluate their models on.

On cost, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1017), Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon form the Pareto frontier: DeepSeek reaches 57.0% pass@1 at $0.04 per rollout, Opus adds ten points at $1.83, and Gemini edges ahead at $3.92.

Harbor can therefore run the whole benchmark straight from the Hugging Face repo, without cloning anything yourself: -k 4 runs 4 attempts per task, and the reported score is the mean reward over all 400 trials.

An agent gets a checkout of a real open-source repository and a short instruction, with the goal of finding and fixing a security weakness without breaking existing functionality. Scoring is fully programmatic, so results are deterministic and anyone can reproduce them without extra cost. All our programmatic checks have been curated with the help of LLM judge panels that shape them towards the direction of hardness and fairness. We also maintain a held-out set , so that we can keep tracking progress on tasks no model has seen. To evaluate your model on the held-out set, contact cyber@collinear.ai .

Our goal is to be exhaustive. A defender has to anticipate the ways an attacker could get in, and get it right every single time. These 100 tasks cover 91 different CWEs, spanning a wide range of vulnerability classes. A model that does well here has to understand the multiple weakness surfaces that a potential attacker can exploit. Recognising a familiar pattern is not enough.

articles.title: Transformers Model Integration Contracts
articles.descEn: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
articles.titleEn: Transformers Model Integration Contracts
summaryLinesEn: 108.6 billion parameters become 44.7 million.
Transformers supports over 750 model types, and its test suite is big: 88,000+ CPU tests on main, plus 200,000+ GPU tests in a daily run.

A Model Integration Contract (MIC) has three parts: a fixture : the shrunk model described above, published once and pinned a usage path : a runnable Markdown example of something people do with the model, such as generating text or running a training step baselines : the outputs recorded when running that example, reviewed by a human The contract holds if running the usage path on the fixture still produces the baselines.

sourceContent.description: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
paragraphs: 108.6 billion parameters become 44.7 million.
Transformers supports over 750 model types, and its test suite is big: 88,000+ CPU tests on main, plus 200,000+ GPU tests in a daily run.

A Model Integration Contract (MIC) has three parts: a fixture : the shrunk model described above, published once and pinned a usage path : a runnable Markdown example of something people do with the model, such as generating text or running a training step baselines : the outputs recorded when running that example, reviewed by a human The contract holds if running the usage path on the fixture still produces the baselines.

On July 30, 2026, Transformers enabled PyTorch's scaled dot-product attention (SDPA) for T5. As a side effect, UMT5's decoder could attend to future tokens. During training, it could peek at the answer it was supposed to predict. Nothing crashed, and the bug stayed in main for almost two months.
When we later replayed those commits, a small UMT5 model running on CPU flagged it on every one of them. This post is about that model and the tests built around it.

Transformers supports over 750 model types, and its test suite is big: 88,000+ CPU tests on main, plus 200,000+ GPU tests in a daily run. Model tests are only part of it: we also test pipelines, training, distributed execution, quantization and attention kernels.

articles.title: Advancing research and partnering with universities in Singapore
articles.descEn: Google is investing in new research grants and capacity-building initiatives to advance AI for science and support the next generation of scientific leaders in Singapore.
articles.titleEn: Advancing research and partnering with universities in Singapore
summaryLinesEn: AI safety and security ($340,000 grant — NTU) : We are funding four sponsored research studies at NTU focused on advancing AI safety frameworks, robust evaluation methodologies, trustworthy multi-agent systems, and privacy-preserving LLM watermarking.

Along with a new research hub in Singapore, Google is deepening its academic partnerships in the country with more than $6 million in grants for NUS and NTU — driving breakthroughs in AI for science and compute efficiency, strengthening AI safety frameworks, and nurturing scientific leaders.

Our targeted grants address both urgent biomedical frontiers and the core building blocks of computing: Alzheimer’s research ($1.5 million grant — NUS) : Selected from over 3,500 global applications, NUS has been awarded an AI for Science Google.org Impact Challenge Grant to advance breakthroughs in neurodegenerative disease research using AI models and data science.

summaryLines: AI 안전 및 보안($340,000 보조금 — NTU): 우리는 AI 안전 프레임워크, 강력한 평가 방법론, 신뢰할 수 있는 다중 에이전트 시스템 및 개인 정보 보호 LLM 워터마킹에 초점을 맞춘 NTU의 4가지 후원 연구 연구에 자금을 지원하고 있음
Google은 싱가포르의 새로운 연구 허브와 함께 NUS 및 NTU에 600만 달러 이상의 보조금을 지원하여 싱가포르 내 학술 파트너십을 심화하여 과학 및 컴퓨팅 효율성을 위한 AI의 혁신을 주도하고 AI 안전 프레임워크를 강화하며 과학 리더를 양성하고 있음
우리의 목표 보조금은 긴급한 생물 의학 분야와 컴퓨팅의 핵심 구성 요소를 모두 다룸 · 알츠하이머 연구(150만 달러 보조금 - NUS): 3,500개 이상의 글로벌 응용 프로그램 중에서 선정된 NUS는 AI 모델과 데이터 과학을 사용하여 신경퇴행성 질환 연구의 획기적인 진전을 이루기 위해 과학용 AI Google.org 임팩트 챌린지 보조금을 받았음

articles.title: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI
articles.descEn: From infrastructure planning and transportation to public services, cities are using NVIDIA-powered applications to address local needs and expand capacity for the broader AI ecosystem.
articles.titleEn: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI
summaryLinesEn: Cities can extend AI to more services by building on infrastructure already in place and adding capacity.

In Wrocław, Poland , K2K is building shared AI infrastructure using NVIDIA accelerated computing, NVIDIA Cosmos world reasoning models, and NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) to transform existing camera streams into actionable intelligence for mobility, safety and event response — using the same infrastructure across several city functions.
City teams don’t need a massive infrastructure investment to get started building these AI services: depending on the workload, NVIDIA RTX workstations or a small GPU system may be enough.

sourceContent.headline: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI
sourceContent.description: From infrastructure planning and transportation to public services, cities are using NVIDIA-powered applications to address local needs and expand capacity for the broader AI ecosystem.
paragraphs: Cities can extend AI to more services by building on infrastructure already in place and adding capacity.

In Wrocław, Poland , K2K is building shared AI infrastructure using NVIDIA accelerated computing, NVIDIA Cosmos world reasoning models, and NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) to transform existing camera streams into actionable intelligence for mobility, safety and event response — using the same infrastructure across several city functions.
City teams don’t need a massive infrastructure investment to get started building these AI services: depending on the workload, NVIDIA RTX workstations or a small GPU system may be enough.
Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge.

Physical and agentic AI offer new ways to close that gap, from digital twins for infrastructure planning to vision and service agents, while keeping local governments in control of how sensitive data is processed and used.

Building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin , NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI and AI agents to cities worldwide. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and local developers a common foundation to build on — extending services without each organization having to acquire and manage resources of their own.

폴란드 브로츠와프에서 K2K는 NVIDIA 가속 컴퓨팅, NVIDIA Cosmos 세계 추론 모델, 비디오 검색 및 요약(VSS)을 위한 NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint를 사용하여 공유 AI 인프라를 구축하고 있으며, 이를 통해 여러 도시 기능에서 동일한 인프라를 사용하여 기존 카메라 스트림을 이동성, 안전 및 이벤트 대응을 위한 실행 가능한 인텔리전스로 변환하고 있음
도시 팀은 이러한 AI 서비스 구축을 시작하기 위해 막대한 인프라 투자가 필요하지 않음 · 워크로드에 따라 NVIDIA RTX 워크스테이션 또는 소형 GPU 시스템이면 충분할 수 있음

articles.title: Designing responsible AI for learning
articles.descEn: Google introduces Guided Learning to Search and Classroom to foster critical thinking. Explore these new AI tools and updated school controls. Get the details.
articles.titleEn: Designing responsible AI for learning
summaryLinesEn: Google Classroom: Starting today, Guided Learning is globally available in Google Classroom, a central hub where teachers and students organize schoolwork, share assignments and stay connected.
We’ll share more specifics with schools in the coming months ahead of the changes rolling out so they have time to prepare and enable a smooth transition.
When a student starts a Guided Learning activity assigned by their teacher, it acts like a 1-1 study tool, anchored in class material to help them stay on task.

articles.title: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It
articles.descEn: An AI-defined fab uses accelerated simulation, learned physics models and AI agents to give engineers faster answers across design, testing and manufacturing.
articles.titleEn: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It
summaryLinesEn: Engineers direct the work and make decisions based on their expertise while spending less time waiting for answers.
Using the NVIDIA cuDSS library, multiphysics simulation software provider COMSOL is accelerating such simulations for semiconductor manufacturing by up to 10x.

Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle.

Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking.

sourceContent.headline: Palette: teaching a small model to build decks in your design language
sourceContent.description: A Blog post by IBM Research on Hugging Face
paragraphs: For example: "Revenue for four quarters, with one clear upward trend.
And because every slide's context is fixed before any code is written, the coder calls run in parallel, one per slide, which makes the coding stage about 6–7× faster.
Both of those point to a model you own: open weights, running on your own infrastructure, trained on your own design language.

Ask a frontier model for a slide deck and you'll get a good one. Ask for ten and they start to look alike: the same tasteful defaults, the same house style, a faint "AI-generated deck" look. That's fine until you want the deck to look like your template. Frontier models have their own house style, and no amount of prompting stops them drifting back to it. And sometimes the content is confidential and can't leave your systems at all.

Both of those point to a model you own: open weights, running on your own infrastructure, trained on your own design language. The catch is that small open models, the kind you'd actually self-host, are bad at this. Their decks come out broken: titles that vanish into the background, text running off the slide, shapes stacked on top of each other.

Palette tests one bet: that a small open-weight model, trained on synthetic data in your design language and checked by a harness, can compete with frontier systems while you keep ownership of the result. We fine-tuned a 20B model to build decks the way people do: a designer plans the deck and a coder draws each slide. Its training data follows the IBM Design Language , and on PresentBench it ranks first on two of the three domains we measured. This post covers how we synthesized the data, trained the model and built a harness around it.

articles.title: Building ultra-low-latency voice AI applications on AWS | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: Learn how Cartesia, an AWS Partner, uses purpose-built State Space Models and AWS infrastructure to deliver sub-100ms text-to-speech and speech-to-text at global scale, and how to deploy its Sonic model on Amazon SageMaker AI or self-managed Amazon EC2 GPU instances.
articles.titleEn: Building ultra-low-latency voice AI applications on AWS | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: Telehealth: Remote patient consultations demand low-latency voice for accurate, empathetic communication.

The demand for real-time voice AI is growing rapidly across industries: Contact centers: AI agents handling millions of customer interactions require instantaneous speech generation to maintain natural dialogue.

Sonic is Cartesia’s flagship streaming text-to-speech model, delivering ultra-realistic speech synthesis with sub-100ms latency: First audio byte in approximately 90ms: Users hear the voice respond almost instantaneously.

Conversational AI is transforming how humans interact with technology. From virtual assistants and AI-powered contact centers to real-time translation and accessibility tools, voice-first interfaces are rapidly becoming the default mode of interaction for millions of users worldwide.

Yet delivering a truly natural voice experience remains one of the hardest challenges in AI infrastructure. Users expect human-like responsiveness. Excess latency can break conversational flow and erode trust. To feel natural, AI-generated speech must arrive within the same temporal window as human turn-taking.

This post introduces how Cartesia , an AWS Partner specializing in real-time voice AI, uses purpose-built State Space Models (SSMs) and AWS infrastructure to deliver sub-100ms text-to-speech and speech-to-text at global scale. Developers can build voice experiences that feel indistinguishable from human conversation.

paragraphs: An agent that reads it as a unit price and multiplies by quantity returns $502,529 for the top customer instead of $27,991.66.
The Stardog post in this series introduced this framing.

An agent that answers business questions from live data needs three layers: a model that plans and writes queries, a meaning layer that tells the agent what the data represents, and a runtime that hosts the agent and controls identity and access.

In this post, we show how to build a semantic layer for agentic AI using EDB Postgres AI . We run a Strands Agents agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that queries the layer to answer customer 360 (C360) questions. AI agents that interact with enterprise APIs on behalf of users need to maintain user identity throughout the request chain. Without identity propagation, API calls arrive at downstream services as the application itself rather than the user who initiated the action. This breaks audit trails, bypasses user-level access controls, and violates the principle of least privilege.

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. This post shows how to configure AgentCore Gateway , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, for an on-behalf-of (OBO) token exchange with Microsoft Entra ID. An AI agent can then call the ServiceNow REST API while preserving the calling user’s identity. You configure the token exchange on the gateway target, and AgentCore Gateway performs the exchange on each request. The pattern can be applied to other REST APIs protected by OAuth.
In production, you can additionally pair identity propagation with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to filter harmful content and validate the agent’s inputs and outputs.

sourceContent.headline: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents
sourceContent.description: A Blog post by Ai2 on Hugging Face
paragraphs: We find that recurrent and hybrid models can generalize much farther than transformers when trained directly on these tasks, while frontier models including Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna still break down on harder forms of state tracking as inputs grow longer.

However, not all state-tracking problems are created equal: some require only finding the latest update; harder ones require following a chain of changes, where one missed step can throw off the final answer.
The models trained on sequences of up to 256 assignments and were tested on sequences as long as 64,000 assignments, or 250 times the maximum training length.
We’re introducing StateBench , a benchmark for long-context state tracking —how well language models keep track of information about entities in long documents as they evolve.

State tracking underlies tasks from reading code, where variables are assigned and reassigned, to following a story as characters physically move around and objects change hands. For example, if a mystery novel states that “John gave Mary the knife” right before a murder occurs, it’s important to know that the state of each character has changed. However, not all state-tracking problems are created equal: some require only finding the latest update; harder ones require following a chain of changes, where one missed step can throw off the final answer. For example, a harder variant of our mystery state tracking would be if John gave Mary the item in his backpack, with it previously known that Edward put a knife in John’s backpack.

Transformers have well-documented theoretical limits on hard variants of state tracking with long dependency chains, helping motivate recurrent and hybrid architectures such as Gated DeltaNet that carry a running memory forward. Existing state-tracking tests tend to focus on the hardest cases, but as these designs become more common, researchers need to know which kinds of state tracking each architecture can handle. We would like to understand the differences between architectures not just on the hardest kinds of state tracking, but also on the simpler, potentially more common kinds.

We’re introducing StateBench , a benchmark for long-context state tracking —how well language models keep track of information about entities in long documents as they evolve.

State tracking underlies tasks from reading code, where variables are assigned and reassigned, to following a story as characters physically move around and objects change hands. For example, if a mystery novel states that “John gave Mary the knife” right before a murder occurs, it’s important to know that the state of each character has changed. However, not all state-tracking problems are created equal: some require only finding the latest update; harder ones require following a chain of changes, where one missed step can throw off the final answer. For example, a harder variant of our mystery state tracking would be if John gave Mary the item in his backpack, with it previously known that Edward put a knife in John’s backpack.

Transformers have well-documented theoretical limits on hard variants of state tracking with long dependency chains, helping motivate recurrent and hybrid architectures such as Gated DeltaNet that carry a running memory forward. Existing state-tracking tests tend to focus on the hardest cases, but as these designs become more common, researchers need to know which kinds of state tracking each architecture can handle. We would like to understand the differences between architectures not just on the hardest kinds of state tracking, but also on the simpler, potentially more common kinds.

articles.descEn: Sharing progress on a powerful type of cryptographic proof known as a zkSNARK, which is uniquely fit for provable inference.
articles.titleEn: Progress on provable inference for large language models
summaryLinesEn: 1 This research post is meant to share intermediate progress, and not a completed research agenda.
Our aim is twofold: (i) accelerating and facilitating the development of provable inference; and (ii) demonstrating that zero-knowledge succinct arguments are practical for provable inference.

Specifically, we have made progress on a powerful type of cryptographic proof known as a “zkSNARK”, which is uniquely fit for provable inference (owing to its strong hiding and efficiency properties).

Frontier Red Team Oct 22, 2026 LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale

Roy Rinberg (Anthropic), Alex Allain (Anthropic); Alessandro Chiesa (EPFL, StarkWare), Miranda Christ (MIT, RESI), Rahul Dalal (Anthropic STEM Fellows Program, Succinct), Giacomo Fenzi (EPFL), Ben Mayer (Anthropic Fellows Program, MIT), Guy Weissenberg (EPFL)

When you talk to a friend in person, you have many ways to know it is really them: you can see them, hear them, shake their hand. When you talk to an AI model, you have almost none. A user querying a model today cannot check that the responses came from the specific model that a developer claims is responding, as opposed to one secretly substituted in by a routing service for cost reasons, or even by an attacker who has tampered with the token stream. Judging from the model’s output alone is unreliable, even if it produces high-quality responses. Cryptographic proofs of inference solve this problem: they let a model provider commit to a model and then prove that each response was produced by that model. Such proofs could enable applications ranging from consumer products to internal security, and could contribute to a toolkit for verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements.

articles.title: Declare and optimize with UNIQUE constraints on Databricks | Databricks Blog
articles.descEn: Databricks UNIQUE constraints let teams declare multiple nullable or composite uniqueness guarantees beyond a table’s single PRIMARY KEY, and reference them with foreign keys.
articles.titleEn: Declare and optimize with UNIQUE constraints on Databricks | Databricks Blog
summaryLinesEn: In 10 TB TPC-DS benchmarks, UNIQUE with RELY removed over 99.99% of shuffle and delivered up to 12× faster queries.
Databricks already supports PRIMARY KEY and FOREIGN KEY constraints : a primary key identifies a table's rows, and foreign keys can reference it to describe relationships.
UNIQUE constraints, now available in Public Preview for Unity Catalog Delta tables in Databricks SQL and Databricks Runtime 18.2 and above, add a way to record the other uniqueness guarantees.

articles.title: Adobe’s Premiere mobile app is adding licensed music from ‘leading artists’
articles.descEn: Adobe is teaming up with Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group to add a library of licensed music clips to the Premiere mobile video editing app.
articles.titleEn: Adobe’s Premiere mobile app is adding licensed music from ‘leading artists’
summaryLinesEn: Adobe is teaming up with Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group to add a library of licensed music clips to the Premiere mobile video editing app.

No specific musicians have been announced with this partnership, but Adobe said it will include “popular songs” from “leading artists,” and enable Premiere mobile users to quickly jump on “the latest trend.”
Adobe says this feature is “coming soon,” and will allow Premiere mobile users to: Add up to 60 seconds of a popular track directly to the video.

articles.title: Apple warns of risks related to AI agents behaving in 'unintended or unpredictable' ways
articles.descEn: Apple’s annual filing warns that AI agents could exceed permissions, resist instructions or take actions that are difficult to reverse.
articles.titleEn: Apple warns of risks related to AI agents behaving in 'unintended or unpredictable' ways
summaryLinesEn: Here's why measuring water usage is hard Nintendo Switch 2 sales plunge 41% as price hikes and memory crunch bite Hyperscalers and Apple surge after election results remove investor uncertainty Separately, the ability of agents to use a computer in human ways is forcing big companies like Amazon and JPMorgan Chase to come up with policies around agentic access to services for strategic or security reasons.
Earlier this year, OpenAI released Dots, and Meta introduced Muse.
The new risk factors in Apple's filing show the disruptive potential of AI agents, which have proliferated across the business world.

articles.title: 地域交通の持続と進化に向けた構造改革
articles.titleEn: 地域交通の持続と進化に向けた構造改革
summaryLinesEn: Ⅰ はじめに Ⅱ モビリティの地域実証が示す方向性 Ⅲ 標準型先進サービスの普及を阻む地域交通の構造的制約 Ⅳ 制約を解く打開策：地域・事業者・制度の枠を超える Ⅴ 交通サービスが持続・進化する構造への転換 Ⅵ さいごに 急速な人口減少により、競争を前提とした生活インフラサービスの維持が困難となり、特に地方の公共交通は量・質が低下する悪循環に陥っている。
NRIフィナンシャル・グラフィックス 戦略マーケティング部 Tel：03-5789-8251（平日9:30～17:00） Fax：03-5789-8254
打開策として、第1に都道府県とMaaS事業者主導の広域連携によるサービスの標準化、第2にM&Aや共同経営による交通事業者の経営基盤の強化、第3に運行委託のバンドル化・成果連動化や事業許可要件の緩和による先進サービスの参入促進が有効である。

Ⅰ はじめに Ⅱ モビリティの地域実証が示す方向性 Ⅲ 標準型先進サービスの普及を阻む地域交通の構造的制約 Ⅳ 制約を解く打開策：地域・事業者・制度の枠を超える Ⅴ 交通サービスが持続・進化する構造への転換 Ⅵ さいごに 急速な人口減少により、競争を前提とした生活インフラサービスの維持が困難となり、特に地方の公共交通は量・質が低下する悪循環に陥っている。
NRIフィナンシャル・グラフィックス 戦略マーケティング部 Tel：03-5789-8251（平日9:30～17:00） Fax：03-5789-8254

sourceContent.headline: 地域交通の持続と進化に向けた構造改革
paragraphs: 急速な人口減少により、競争を前提とした生活インフラサービスの維持が困難となり、特に地方の公共交通は量・質が低下する悪循環に陥っている。厳しい環境でサービスを持続させるには、地域特性によらず導入できる標準的な先進サービスを構築し横展開することで、地域当たりの負担を低減することが目指すべき方向性である。
NRIフィナンシャル・グラフィックス 戦略マーケティング部 Tel：03-5789-8251（平日9:30～17:00） Fax：03-5789-8254
打開策として、第1に都道府県とMaaS事業者主導の広域連携によるサービスの標準化、第2にM&Aや共同経営による交通事業者の経営基盤の強化、第3に運行委託のバンドル化・成果連動化や事業許可要件の緩和による先進サービスの参入促進が有効である。
地域交通には、標準型先進サービスの普及を阻む3つの制約がある。自治体単位で交通施策が分断されている「地域別のサイロ化」、運行主体が小規模で投資余力が限られる「事業者の分散」、事業者を固定化し新規参入を妨げる「事業展開の規制」による制約を解く必要がある。

sourceContent.headline: 「売り切り製造業」から「人の生活とつながる産業」へ
paragraphs: 人口減少下の日本が持続的成長を実現するには、地方の雇用や波及効果に優れる製造業の強化が不可欠である。しかし「よいモノを、より多く、より安く」供給する従来型のビジネスモデルは、新興国や中国の供給圧力の中で限界を迎えている。求められるのは、製品を売り切る発想から脱却し、製品を通じて築いた顧客基盤を土台に、生活・業務全体へ価値提供を広げるビジネスモデルへの転換である。

名前 山田 昌輝 所属・職名 アーバンイノベーションコンサルティング部 地域イノベーショングループ シニアコンサルタント 名前 井上 海 所属・職名 アーバンイノベーションコンサルティング部 地域イノベーショングループ シニアコンサルタント 名前 吉川 貴城 所属・職名 アーバンイノベーションコンサルティング部 地域イノベーショングループ コンサルタント NRIフィナンシャル・グラフィックス 戦略マーケティング部 Tel：03-5789-8251（平日9:30～17:00） Fax：03-5789-8254
Ⅰ はじめに：日本の成長を支える製造業の再定義 Ⅱ 自動車産業の競争構造の変化 Ⅲ SDV2.0の市場実装 Ⅳ 「生活エージェント」となるSDV2.0がもたらす価値 Ⅴ 「つなぐ」ことで変わる製造業のビジネスモデル

その転換を象徴するのが自動車産業である。EV化・SDV化により、競争軸は「販売時点の完成度」から「販売後も価値を更新し続ける力」へと移り、既存のOEMは厳しい立場にある。本稿では長期の視点から、車両が自律的に稼働し、送迎・買い物代行・見守りといった生活タスクそのものを物理的に代替する段階を「SDV2.0」と定義する。この領域では、車両を動かし続ける「稼働保証力」と外部事業者を束ねる「エコシステム運営力」が競争優位の源泉となる。OEMとしては、生活タスクの代替対価や事業者からの手数料を継続的に得るプラットフォーム型モデルへの発展が期待できる。

summaryLinesEn: 昭和から平成前半における経済の拡大期に築かれた事業構造や制度設計は、そのままでは機能しにくくなっていることは明らかである。

それ以降の約20年を振り返ってみると、金融危機（いわゆるリーマンショック）による経済の落ち込みに始まり、中国を中心とした新興国経済の急拡大、さらに、東京オリンピック特需といったような、特定事象によって大きく影響を受けた局面が相次いだ。
NRIフィナンシャル・グラフィックス 戦略マーケティング部 Tel：03-5789-8251（平日9:30～17:00） Fax：03-5789-8254

日本の人口は、2008年に減少へ転じた。それ以降の約20年を振り返ってみると、金融危機（いわゆるリーマンショック）による経済の落ち込みに始まり、中国を中心とした新興国経済の急拡大、さらに、東京オリンピック特需といったような、特定事象によって大きく影響を受けた局面が相次いだ。一方、人口減少の加速によって需要が成熟し、人手不足が常態化する中で、国内ではその流れを食い止めるような構造変化は見られなかった。昭和から平成前半における経済の拡大期に築かれた事業構造や制度設計は、そのままでは機能しにくくなっていることは明らかである。したがって今後は収縮する社会を前提に、産業や公共サービスの仕組みを大胆に組み替える段階に入ってくる。

最近、中国で最先端のフィジカルAIロボットを見る機会があった。幾つかの種類のロボットを見たが、その中でもUnitree社の製品の運動能力は素晴らしく、人間との会話もできる性能を兼ね備えていた。ロボット自体の進化にも大変驚かされたが、さらに驚かされたのは、そのロボットを活用してサービスを提供する企業が多数存在し、サービス内容を競い合っている点である。中国では共働きの家庭が多く、少子高齢化も進んでいるため、家事や介護に必要な動作をトレーニングし、家庭に派遣することを計画する企業も多く存在する。このことは、ハードウエアとしてのロボットを製造する専門企業と、具体的なサービスとして展開する企業との間で水平分業が確立されつつあることを意味する。

PlanAssist - an AI planning tool that handles the heavy lifting of routine applications so officers can focus their expertise where it matters most - is to be made available to an additional 12 local planning authorities across England.

In early pilot testing across Barnet, Camden, and Dorset, PlanAssist showed it could bring the average time a planning officer spent on householder assessment tasks down by 58%. Designed to support human judgement, the tool speeds up routine checks while ensuring planning officers retain the final say on every application.

articles.descEn: Two results show how Claude helps life sciences researchers speed up their work: designing protein binders from scratch and analyzing NMR and LC-MS data to speed chemical analysis.

summaryLinesEn: The protein design and analytical chemistry tasks described below are representative of the work that makes up some parts of the early stages of the drug development process.

Accelerating these phases is one component of our much larger effort to speed up drug development end-to-end, many aspects of which have more to do with policy and operational bottlenecks than with improvements in core scientific capabilities.
Second, we share how Claude Opus 5 performed on an analytical chemistry task, demonstrating how general-access models can support the routine and time-intensive aspects of research.

AI models are also beginning to hasten progress in experimental fields where verifying the results is more complex and expensive, such as in the life sciences. In this post, we share the results of two experiments into Claude’s scientific capabilities. First, we present findings from our investigation into Claude’s performance on a protein design campaign, showing that Claude can design protein binders against a variety of targets as well as (or even better than) leading human experts. Second, we share how Claude Opus 5 performed on an analytical chemistry task, demonstrating how general-access models can support the routine and time-intensive aspects of research.

articles.title: Claude-shaped science
articles.descEn: Matthew Schwartz describes what happened when he stopped fighting Claude and allowed Claude to find “Claude-shaped” problems. This led him to build BootLoops, a toolkit for exact calculations in quantitative science, which he has been applying across scientific fields alongside experts.
articles.titleEn: Claude-shaped science
summaryLinesEn: Knowing where the amplitude is infinite (its “singularities”) might narrow it to 20,000 options; a symmetry cuts that to 500; and so on down to one.
Matthew Schwartz returns to describe a new approach to AI-accelerated science.
Because similar calculations often turn up across very disparate areas of science, Claude found connections to ecology, population genetics, and a dozen other fields.

sourceContent.headline: Claude-shaped science
sourceContent.description: Matthew Schwartz describes what happened when he stopped fighting Claude and allowed Claude to find “Claude-shaped” problems. This led him to build BootLoops, a toolkit for exact calculations in quantitative science, which he has been applying across scientific fields alongside experts.
paragraphs: Knowing where the amplitude is infinite (its “singularities”) might narrow it to 20,000 options; a symmetry cuts that to 500; and so on down to one.
Matthew Schwartz returns to describe a new approach to AI-accelerated science.
Because similar calculations often turn up across very disparate areas of science, Claude found connections to ecology, population genetics, and a dozen other fields.

In this guest post, Prof. Matthew Schwartz returns to describe a new approach to AI-accelerated science. In Vibe Physics , Schwartz discussed similarities in capability between Claude and a physics graduate student. Here, he describes what happened when he stopped fighting Claude and allowed Claude to find “Claude-shaped” problems: ones best suited to the capabilities of the current generation of LLM tools. This led him to build BootLoops, a toolkit for exact calculations in quantitative science. Because similar calculations often turn up across very disparate areas of science, Claude found connections to ecology, population genetics, and a dozen other fields. These connections were often technically correct but scientifically unremarkable at first, so Schwartz worked with domain experts to steer BootLoops toward questions those fields care about. Below, we share more about these projects and how BootLoops came about.
Science Oct 16, 2026 Designing more efficient quantum circuits with Claude

Agentic AI is improving rapidly. Everyone notices the models seem smarter: they know more, make fewer mistakes, and have better ideas. If you follow the trend lines, it is easy to speak confidently about the potential of AI to revolutionize science. However, academic scientists trying to use the models today in their own work often feel a disconnect. The models may be solving challenging and longstanding problems , but so far these have mostly been well-scoped applications of existing techniques. Many of the headlines seem to be in mathematics, the one part of science where a problem can be stated completely and an answer checked absolutely. But most of science is not like that. And for many of us researchers and students, the distance between those headlines and what happens when we use these models can leave us frustrated and anxious.

articles.title: The AI-native marketing org: Six functions that need to get done
articles.descEn: The AI-native marketing org rests on six functions: four human, two agent-owned. Diego Lomanto on how to reshape roles without a reorg.
articles.titleEn: The AI-native marketing org: Six functions that need to get done
summaryLinesEn: The data backs this up: 70% of CMOs say becoming an AI leader is a critical goal, but only 30% report the organizational readiness to actually scale it .
And that shift has to show up in what the org rewards.
Six functions every marketing org needs to perform in an AI-native world .
articles.summary:
The data backs this up: 70% of CMOs say becoming an AI leader is a critical goal, but only 30% report the organizational readiness to actually scale it .

Six functions every marketing org needs to perform in an AI-native world .

sourceContent.headline: The AI-native marketing org: Six functions that need to get done
sourceContent.description: The AI-native marketing org rests on six functions: four human, two agent-owned. Diego Lomanto on how to reshape roles without a reorg.
paragraphs: The data backs this up: 70% of CMOs say becoming an AI leader is a critical goal, but only 30% report the organizational readiness to actually scale it .
And that shift has to show up in what the org rewards.
Six functions every marketing org needs to perform in an AI-native world .
In the last year, I’ve watched marketing roles change faster than at any point in my career. Not in theory: in practice, on my own team at WRITER and on the teams of the companies we work with.

A content manager who used to write 10 blog posts a month now curates the system that writes 50. A campaign manager who used to build one campaign at a time now orchestrates five in parallel, directing agents instead of drafting copy . A brand strategist who used to be in every approval meeting now encodes the brand standards once and lets agents reproduce them across every output. The org chart and titles remain the same, but the work and the rewards shift radically.
Most of their organizations haven’t noticed. The org chart looks the same. The performance reviews measure the same things. The budget still flows to whoever produces the most volume.

articles.title: Key findings from our 2025 enterprise AI adoption report
articles.descEn: Key findings from our 2025 enterprise AI adoption report reveal the benefits and challenges of implementing AI.
articles.titleEn: Key findings from our 2025 enterprise AI adoption report
summaryLinesEn: For our 2025 report, Generative AI adoption in the enterprise, we surveyed a diverse group of 1,600 knowledge workers actively using AI in the workplace — including 800 C-suite executives and 800 employees across the US.

Despite clear benefits, enterprise leaders report division and power struggles from AI adoption While executives are highly optimistic about the future business impact of AI, 42% say the process of adopting generative AI is tearing their company apart.
Enterprises without a formal AI strategy report only 37% success in AI adoption, compared to 80% for those with a strategy.

sourceContent.headline: Key findings from our 2025 enterprise AI adoption report
sourceContent.description: Key findings from our 2025 enterprise AI adoption report reveal the benefits and challenges of implementing AI.
paragraphs: For our 2025 report, Generative AI adoption in the enterprise, we surveyed a diverse group of 1,600 knowledge workers actively using AI in the workplace — including 800 C-suite executives and 800 employees across the US.

Despite clear benefits, enterprise leaders report division and power struggles from AI adoption While executives are highly optimistic about the future business impact of AI, 42% say the process of adopting generative AI is tearing their company apart.
Enterprises without a formal AI strategy report only 37% success in AI adoption, compared to 80% for those with a strategy.

Optimism around AI is increasing, yet nearly two out of three C-suite executives report that generative AI adoption has sparked division within their organizations — 42% state that it’s tearing their companies apart.
Success lies in a people-first approach . Companies that are getting it right are appointing AI champions, making strategic investments, and developing a comprehensive AI strategy.

The research was conducted in partnership with research group Workplace Intelligence to provide a deeper understanding of the opportunities and barriers to adoption in the enterprise.

articles.descEn: Discover HFS Research’s new framework for trusted, enterprise-grade LLMs and learn how WRITER’s agent supervision suite and Palmyra X5 model help CIOs govern and scale agentic AI safely across the business.
articles.titleEn: From chaos to control: why enterprises need a new framework for trusted LLMs
summaryLinesEn: Today, 75% of knowledge workers use GenAI at work, but only about a third of organizations have formal AI governance in place For CIOs, this creates a familiar and uncomfortable reality: AI enthusiasm is accelerating faster than enterprise readiness.

articles.title: How Arm is redefining the PC ecosystem
articles.descEn: Discover how Arm-based PCs are transforming personal computing through new agentic AI capabilities and a growing native software ecosystem.

summaryLinesEn: The growth of Arm-based PCs reflects years of investment in silicon innovation, software compatibility, native applications and ecosystem collaboration.

This post walks through the architecture, the initial Amazon Bedrock Flows implementation, the migration to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the lessons learned from scaling it.

This post was co-written with Marek Klatowicz, Cloud DevOps Engineer at Circle K.

Many DevOps teams know the incident triage pattern: An alert fires, and before anyone can fix the problem, an engineer spends 45–60 minutes figuring out what happened. They pull logs, check service health, and correlate symptoms across a handful of tools. All of this happens before remediation can begin.

At Circle K, this challenge scaled with the business. The company operates more than 17,200 convenience and fuel retail stores across 27 countries. Behind the storefronts, a cloud-native infrastructure supports point-of-sale systems, loyalty applications, and electric vehicle (EV) charging applications running on AWS. As the company expanded its digital operations, the triage overhead grew with it. More services meant more alerts, and each one required the same manual investigation before remediation could begin.

sourceContent.description: Learn how to build a multi-agent engineering assistant that compresses aerospace component substitution evaluation from days to minutes, using Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the Strands Agents SDK to assemble substitution evidence while keeping the engineer as the decision-maker.
paragraphs: Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings appears in two distinct roles: Multimodal retrieval – Datasheets, ICDs, and performance charts are embedded with Nova Multimodal Embeddings so text and visual content share one semantic space.

When a qualified aerospace component goes obsolete or hits a long lead time, an engineer spends days cross-referencing specifications across vendor datasheets, interface control documents (ICDs), and qualification records before documenting a substitution justification for review. An incorrect substitution on a flight-critical component can cause mission failure, yet the evidence trail behind each decision is often spread across email and undocumented institutional knowledge, so there is no formal, repeatable package for a reviewer to check.

A previous post, Manufacturing intelligence with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings , showed how the model retrieves answers locked inside engineering diagrams, thermal plots, and datasheet charts that text-only pipelines miss. This post picks up where that retrieval work left off, putting those capabilities inside a multi-agent system that assembles substitution evidence, from retrieval to a drafted assessment.

In this post, we show how to build a multi-agent engineering assistant that cuts the manual cross-referencing behind part substitution evaluation using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore , Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings , and the open source Strands Agents SDK . A planner routes work across three specialist agents that search a multimodal knowledge base, score candidates against deterministic tolerance rules, compare part photos, and ground lifecycle claims in live web data. The engineer remains the decision-maker throughout, because the system assembles evidence and drafts documents without ever approving a substitution on its own.

articles.title: Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: Agentic assistants built on frontier models run a multi-step tool loop, and paying frontier prices on every step is hard to sustain at production scale. This post shows how to use sequence-level knowledge distillation (SeqKD) to transfer a frontier teacher's agentic behavior into a small, lower-cost student on Amazon SageMaker AI.
articles.titleEn: Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: It searches the catalog of about 2.7 million products, inspects candidates, and recommends the ones that meet the constraints.
At production scale, that per-task cost compounds, erodes the project’s ROI, and stops the project from shipping.

Knowledge distillation closes that gap by transferring the behavior of the larger “teacher” model into a smaller “student”, training the student to reproduce the teacher’s outputs, so it keeps much of the quality at the smaller model’s speed and cost.
