sourceContent.headline: Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI | Amazon Web Services
sourceContent.description: Agentic assistants built on frontier models run a multi-step tool loop, and paying frontier prices on every step is hard to sustain at production scale. This post shows how to use sequence-level knowledge distillation (SeqKD) to transfer a frontier teacher's agentic behavior into a small, lower-cost student on Amazon SageMaker AI.
paragraphs: It searches the catalog of about 2.7 million products, inspects candidates, and recommends the ones that meet the constraints.
At production scale, that per-task cost compounds, erodes the project’s ROI, and stops the project from shipping.

Knowledge distillation closes that gap by transferring the behavior of the larger “teacher” model into a smaller “student”, training the student to reproduce the teacher’s outputs, so it keeps much of the quality at the smaller model’s speed and cost.

You built a shopping assistant on a frontier model, and it works. A shopper asks for “a black waist bag under twenty dollars from a shop with at least 4.5 stars,” and the agent searches the catalog, inspects candidates, checks the constraints, and commits to a recommendation. But what does that interaction actually cost? An agentic assistant is not one model call, it is a loop: search, read results, refine, verify, decide. A single completed task can be multiple calls to that frontier model, and you pay for every one, on every shopper. At production scale, that per-task cost compounds, erodes the project’s ROI, and stops the project from shipping.

One way to make an agentic application more efficient is to use a smaller model, which is faster to respond and more cost-effective to host. The catch is quality: a smaller model usually falls short on the task, which is why the larger one was chosen in the first place. Knowledge distillation closes that gap by transferring the behavior of the larger “teacher” model into a smaller “student”, training the student to reproduce the teacher’s outputs, so it keeps much of the quality at the smaller model’s speed and cost.

In this post you will learn how to use knowledge distillation, and specifically sequence-level knowledge distillation (SeqKD), to fine-tune a shopping agent on Amazon SageMaker AI . We cover how to generate high-quality multi-step trajectories with a frontier teacher and keep the ones that solve the task, how to encode them for supervised fine-tuning, how to run the training on serverless infrastructure, and how to evaluate the student against a held-out benchmark.

articles.title: Prepare web content for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Crawl4AI | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: This post shows how to use Crawl4AI, an open source web crawler, as a content preparation layer for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, handling JavaScript rendering, selective extraction, and custom metadata enrichment before web content reaches an Amazon S3 data source.
articles.titleEn: Prepare web content for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Crawl4AI | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: Because managed and customer-managed knowledge bases both support Amazon S3 data sources, the Crawl4AI path works with either type.

The module src/crawl4ai_bedrock_kb/crawl.py contains the complete seed pacing, URL filtering and scoping, page limits, and redirect checks: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases supports several document formats for Amazon S3 data sources, including plain text, HTML, Markdown, PDF, and DOCX.
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases is the fully managed RAG capability of Amazon Bedrock.

The module src/crawl4ai_bedrock_kb/crawl.py contains the complete seed pacing, URL filtering and scoping, page limits, and redirect checks: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases supports several document formats for Amazon S3 data sources, including plain text, HTML, Markdown, PDF, and DOCX.
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases is the fully managed RAG capability of Amazon Bedrock.

When you build Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) applications, answer quality depends on the data that you ingest. Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases is the fully managed RAG capability of Amazon Bedrock. With Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base , you connect your data sources, and Amazon Bedrock manages ingestion, storage, indexing, and retrieval for you. You don’t provision or scale a vector store, and embedding and reranking use service-managed models by default.

For web content, start with the Amazon Bedrock Web Crawler data source connector for managed knowledge bases. You give it the seed URLs or sitemaps that you’re authorized to crawl, and it crawls within the scope and rate limits that you set. Scheduled syncs keep your knowledge base current as pages change, and the connector can wait for content that loads with JavaScript. There’s no crawler for you to build, host, or operate, so this connector is the starting point for most public website content.

Some sources need more control over what reaches the knowledge base. You might want to index only the main content region of each page, remove navigation and other boilerplate, or attach your own metadata attributes to every document. For that class of source material, you can extend the reach of your knowledge base with a preparation step built with Crawl4AI , an open source Python crawler. The step writes Markdown and a metadata sidecar for each page to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), and the knowledge base ingests both through its Amazon S3 data source.

articles.title: Redesigning Agent Studio around Ghostwriter
articles.descEn: We’ve redesigned Agent Studio around Ghostwriter, so you can go from asking why resolution rates dropped to examining the conversations, updating a journey, and testing the fix — all in one conversation.
articles.titleEn: Redesigning Agent Studio around Ghostwriter
summaryLinesEn: Agent Studio now brings related agents into a single project, along with the data and channels they share, so your team can test and release them together.

Ghostwriter is our agent for building agents — an always-on teammate that not only helps you build but also understands how agents are performing, suggests improvements in Slack and Teams, and pushes whatever you approve live.
When the lender adds a new document requirement, Ghostwriter updates what the first agent asks for and how the second one follows up, all in one session.

articles.title: The Platform Behind the Next AI Breakthrough
articles.descEn: How AI-optimized infrastructure turns model innovation into lasting business impact.
articles.titleEn: The Platform Behind the Next AI Breakthrough
summaryLinesEn: Compute must respond to the changing demand of agentic workloads.
They can write and validate code, coordinate across systems, rebalance inventory as conditions change, manage production operations, or carry a migration from plan to completion.
Teams need a complete view of performance, capacity, and cost so they can find bottlenecks and improve the full workload instead of tuning one component at a time.
articles.summary:
Compute must respond to the changing demand of agentic workloads.
They can write and validate code, coordinate across systems, rebalance inventory as conditions change, manage production operations, or carry a migration from plan to completion.
Teams need a complete view of performance, capacity, and cost so they can find bottlenecks and improve the full workload instead of tuning one component at a time.

sourceContent.headline: The Platform Behind the Next AI Breakthrough
sourceContent.description: How AI-optimized infrastructure turns model innovation into lasting business impact.
paragraphs: Compute must respond to the changing demand of agentic workloads.
They can write and validate code, coordinate across systems, rebalance inventory as conditions change, manage production operations, or carry a migration from plan to completion.
Teams need a complete view of performance, capacity, and cost so they can find bottlenecks and improve the full workload instead of tuning one component at a time.

The next frontier of AI is coming into focus as agents take on longer, more strategic work. They can write and validate code, coordinate across systems, rebalance inventory as conditions change, manage production operations, or carry a migration from plan to completion. AI is no longer supporting one step; it is executing and reshaping the process itself.

New models help drive this change by expanding what AI can reason about, create, and accomplish. But the combination of advances in models and infrastructure is key to moving agents from isolated tasks to sustained, high-impact work. Realizing that potential requires silicon, compute, storage, and networking to work together so workloads run faster and more reliably at scale.

Cloud infrastructure has evolved before to support new kinds of applications. Even the most advanced cloud-native applications often followed predictable request-and-response paths. To deliver this at scale, cloud-native architectures turned to containers, distributed services, and dynamic scaling, to make the platform more automated and flexible. Agentic applications build on that foundation but introduce another shift: long-running work whose path and resource needs are dynamic and often unpredictable.

sourceContent.headline: From AI models to deployment: Five developer takeaways shaping the future of AI
sourceContent.description: Discover five key developer takeaways shaping the future of AI, from model optimization and agentic AI to deployment across cloud, edge, and physical environments.
paragraphs: Bridging the ExecuTorch Adoption Gap Through Developer Learning ” addressed how developers can move from familiar PyTorch workflows toward on-device deployment.
Speech audio stayed local, while transcripts, commands, and event information moved between systems.
Here are the five takeaways from the events and what they mean for the future of AI applications.

Building an AI model is only one step toward delivering an AI application. Developers need to determine where intelligence runs, how it interacts with other systems, and how to maintain performance and reliability as applications evolve.

That challenge connected WeAreDevelopers World Congress North America in September with October’s Arm Create event at PyTorch, the PyTorch Conference, AGNTCon + MCPCon, and GitHub Universe events. Together, they traced the developer journey from building and optimizing models to orchestrating intelligent applications, then testing, deploying, and scaling software, through a variety of demos, presentations, partner-led sessions, and hands-on workshops.

Arm’s contributions across all these events focused on connecting the common Arm compute foundation spanning cloud, edge and physical environments with open frameworks, model optimization, device interoperability, and performance analysis. The common goal was to help developers move from individual AI capabilities to applications they could build, evaluate, and deploy.

articles.title: New AI-driven Windows malware feeds stolen data to Claude to rank victims’ assets by value, then deletes itself — payload builds custom target assessment, can switch models if one refuses, or skip the AI step entirely
articles.descEn: Stolen Gmail receipts and food-delivery orders feed an AI request for a ‘target assessment’ of each victim.
articles.titleEn: New AI-driven Windows malware feeds stolen data to Claude to rank victims’ assets by value, then deletes itself — payload builds custom target assessment, can switch models if one refuses, or skip the AI step entirely
summaryLinesEn: Already, a Windows malware implant reported in September was built around a panel of up to four LLMs that vote on its next move, and another, reported this week, can fall back to using the victim’s own OpenAI API key.

The target should revoke or rotate all API keys and tokens and change passwords, regardless of exposure; likewise, any funds in a wallet whose seed phrase was stored in plaintext should be moved to a new wallet with a fresh seed, preferably generated on an air-gapped device.
Operating systems need a defensive AI built-in, of course they must be working on this already...

sourceContent.description: Stolen Gmail receipts and food-delivery orders feed an AI request for a ‘target assessment’ of each victim.
paragraphs: Already, a Windows malware implant reported in September was built around a panel of up to four LLMs that vote on its next move, and another, reported this week, can fall back to using the victim’s own OpenAI API key.

Already, a Windows malware implant reported in September was built around a panel of up to four LLMs that vote on its next move, and another, reported this week, can fall back to using the victim’s own OpenAI API key.
Stolen Gmail receipts and food-delivery orders feed an AI request for a ‘target assessment’ of each victim.

A self-deleting Windows infostealer that calls itself VOLTA-AUTODOXER steals everything it can from a victim’s PC, then asks an AI model, Anthropic’s Claude by default, to turn the haul into a target assessment, Cisco’s Talos research organization reports . The malware builds a structured “evidence bundle” on the person and asks the model for a list of their valuables ranked by how much they could be cashed out for, to see what’s worth the effort. VOLTA operates with a prompt to act as “a forensic intelligence analyst” and to be “blunt, specific, accurate,” and can switch models if one refuses, or even do without.

VOLTA steals browser passwords, cookies, and saved payment cards, Thunderbird and Outlook email profiles, Roblox accounts, Microsoft OAuth tokens, screenshots, and even SSH and cloud-provider configuration files. Every saved Wi-Fi password gets pulled in plaintext. Cryptocurrency wallets, when present, are not just copied, as the malware attempts to crack their vaults inline. It then builds the evidence bundle on the person: geolocation and home address, employer and employer domain, inferred birth year, document authorship metadata, and the last four digits of their payment cards.

articles.titleEn: Enabling independent research on how people use Claude
summaryLinesEn: This spring, we piloted a program in which three external research institutions designed and ran their own studies on Claude usage data through Anthropic Insights (formerly named ‘Clio’), the privacy-preserving tool our own teams use to analyze usage patterns across millions of Claude conversations.

Earlier this year, we ran a pilot giving external researchers access to aggregate, real-world Claude usage data. Three research groups designed their own studies for Anthropic Insights, our privacy-preserving analysis tool; we ran the data collection on their behalf, and they conducted their own independent analysis. In this post, we share high-level results from those studies and what we learned running this pilot. We’re also providing an expression of interest form for researchers who may want to work with us in the future.
Societal Impacts Sep 29, 2026 What do you want from AI?

Ensuring the transition to transformative AI goes well requires understanding its impact on people and society. Right now, data on real-world interactions with AI is concentrated in a handful of labs. We think it would be good if more data was made widely available—to researchers, policymakers, and the general public.

articles.title: Lakebase branching for CI/CD: lessons from 100 PR databases | Databricks Blog
articles.descEn: Snorkel’s CI provisions an ephemeral Kubernetes environment for every open PR and ad-hoc commit, and each namespace greatly benefits from a near-instant access to a full secure copy of the production database with Lakebase branching.
articles.titleEn: Lakebase branching for CI/CD: lessons from 100 PR databases | Databricks Blog
summaryLinesEn: The alternatives (shared staging databases, trimmed fixtures, or synthetic data) bring back the problems production-like testing is supposed to solve: tests interfering with each other, stale schemas, and bugs that only show up with real data shapes.

Snorkel AI's CI/CD pipeline gives every open pull request its own Lakebase Postgres branch, a full read/write copy of production data that's ready in under a minute instead of over 30 minutes or longer, due to which they were never able to enable copy per PR.
Lakebase branches are copy-on-write, so 100 concurrent PR databases on a ~2.5 TB production dataset only add storage for the data each branch changes.

Weaviate v1.40 is now available open-source and on Weaviate Cloud .

Two features reach general availability in this release: dropping a named vector , which frees the disk and index memory an unused vector was holding, and 4-bit Rotational Quantization . Two more are new: the HFresh index now takes multi-vector embeddings through MUVERA, and PathSeer joins ACORN and sweeping as a third filter strategy for HNSW. This post also catches up on the Search REST API , which changed a lot over the 1.39 patch line. It also covers a breaking change to vector configuration defaults to check before you upgrade.
If your server sets DEFAULT_VECTORIZER_MODULE , read Vector configuration defaults before you upgrade.

articles.title: Stripe on Stripe: What we learned moving $1B in vendor payments to Global Payouts
articles.descEn: In early 2026, we began moving our vendor payments to Global Payouts, Stripe’s product for paying recipients in 160+ countries. New-market setup fell from six weeks to one, with a 99.9% payout success rate. Here’s what we learned.
articles.titleEn: Stripe on Stripe: What we learned moving $1B in vendor payments to Global Payouts
summaryLinesEn: By October 2026, we had paid over $1 billion to more than 3,400 vendors in the US and UK using Global Payouts.
Once we identified the most common reasons for failure, we moved those checks earlier in the payment flow.

sourceContent.headline: Stripe on Stripe: What we learned moving $1B in vendor payments to Global Payouts
sourceContent.description: In early 2026, we began moving our vendor payments to Global Payouts, Stripe’s product for paying recipients in 160+ countries. New-market setup fell from six weeks to one, with a 99.9% payout success rate. Here’s what we learned.
paragraphs: By October 2026, we had paid over $1 billion to more than 3,400 vendors in the US and UK using Global Payouts.
Once we identified the most common reasons for failure, we moved those checks earlier in the payment flow.
Earlier this year, we began moving Stripe’s own vendor payments to the product we were building to help our users send money around the world: Stripe Global Payouts .

Stripe makes nearly 20,000 payments to vendors in more than 70 markets a year. Historically, we’ve made those payments through direct bank integrations connected to our enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. Where we didn’t have an integration, teams had to manually enter payments through bank portals.

That system worked but grew harder to support as Stripe scaled. Every banking relationship came with its own technical, contractual, and security requirements, and it took weeks to build an integration for a new market. When a payment failed, our operations and finance teams had to search across bank portals and the ERP to identify the problem and resend the money.

Earlier this year, we began moving Stripe’s own vendor payments to the product we were building to help our users send money around the world: Stripe Global Payouts . Global Payouts enables businesses to pay recipients in more than 160 countries through a single API using local bank transfers, international wires, and stablecoins without requiring recipients to open a Stripe account.

articles.title: 「不安なのに、何もしていない」住まい・暮らし方にみる生活者の防犯意識
articles.titleEn: 「不安なのに、何もしていない」住まい・暮らし方にみる生活者の防犯意識
summaryLinesEn: 防犯に不安を感じている層は44.4%に達する一方、自主的な防犯対策を「特に何もしていない」は54.3%と半数を超える。
持ち家（一戸建て）では不安層が54.7%と半数を超える一方、持ち家（マンションなど集合住宅）では30.5%にとどまり、「あまり＋まったく不安を感じていない」（43.8%）を下回る。
また、共働きなどで「ほぼ毎日（週5回以上）」留守になる層では33.1%と、在宅者のいる留守が「ほとんどない」層（28.6%）よりやや高い。

sourceContent.headline: 「不安なのに、何もしていない」住まい・暮らし方にみる生活者の防犯意識
paragraphs: 防犯に不安を感じている層は44.4%に達する一方、自主的な防犯対策を「特に何もしていない」は54.3%と半数を超える。
持ち家（一戸建て）では不安層が54.7%と半数を超える一方、持ち家（マンションなど集合住宅）では30.5%にとどまり、「あまり＋まったく不安を感じていない」（43.8%）を下回る。
また、共働きなどで「ほぼ毎日（週5回以上）」留守になる層では33.1%と、在宅者のいる留守が「ほとんどない」層（28.6%）よりやや高い。
野村総合研究所（NRI）は2026年8月、関東1都6県に住む満15～69歳を対象に、自宅の防犯に関するアンケート調査を行った。防犯に不安を感じている層は44.4%に達する一方、自主的な防犯対策を「特に何もしていない」は54.3%と半数を超える。防犯は「気にはなっているが、行動には移していない」領域となっている。
不安と行動の表れ方は住居形態によって異なる。不安層は持ち家（一戸建て）で54.7%、持ち家（マンションなど集合住宅）で30.5%と、20ポイント以上の差がある。戸建ては自主的な防犯対策の実施率も最も高い「自衛型」、分譲マンションは建物側の設備や管理体制に委ねる傾向がみられる。賃貸集合住宅は、原状回復の制約などから自ら手を加えにくい状況にある。
ホームセキュリティの契約率は7.6%で、未導入理由は戸建てでは「料金が高そう」が62.1%、集合住宅では「導入できないと思う」が最も多い。「自分には必要ないと思う」はいずれの住居形態でも1割未満にとどまる。

articles.title: Our customers’ ambition is accelerating our growth
articles.descEn: We launched Sierra just over two and a half years ago. This week, we hit $400M+ in ARR, adding $150M+ in ARR in Q3 alone. That’s more ARR in one quarter than we generated all of last year.

summaryLinesEn: This week, we hit $400M+ in ARR, adding over $150M+ in ARR in Q3 alone.
More importantly, our growth is accelerating: we took six months to double from $100M to $200M ARR, and only five months to double from $200M to $400M.

This growth is driven by a number of different factors, including: The increasing ambition of our customers — while being some of the largest and most heavily regulated businesses in the world, they’re pushing to do more with their agents, faster.

articles.title: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
articles.descEn: Scientists at the Allen Telescope Array have integrated the NVIDIA Holoscan platform to search for signals that may come from aliens — or the AI they built.
articles.titleEn: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
summaryLinesEn: Radio telescopes generate enormous volumes of data, creating a challenge for scientists who need to identify potentially interesting signals as observations unfold.
Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence.
The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies.

sourceContent.headline: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
sourceContent.description: Scientists at the Allen Telescope Array have integrated the NVIDIA Holoscan platform to search for signals that may come from aliens — or the AI they built.
paragraphs: Radio telescopes generate enormous volumes of data, creating a challenge for scientists who need to identify potentially interesting signals as observations unfold.
Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence.
The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies.

While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents built by aliens.

Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. Such civilizations might have developed technologies far beyond humanity’s, including forms of AI.

Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence. At the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, agents can now steer the instrument, enhance and correct incoming data, and apply AI models to the incoming stream — all from a single natural language request. The NVIDIA Holoscan platform processes the massive streams of sensor data, giving agents live data to act on.

articles.title: Scaling Managed Agents with stable interfaces
articles.descEn: Harnesses encode assumptions that go stale as models improve. See how Managed Agents is built around interfaces that stay stable as harnesses change.
articles.titleEn: Scaling Managed Agents with stable interfaces
summaryLinesEn: As just one example, in prior work we found that Claude Sonnet 4.5 would wrap up tasks prematurely as it sensed its context limit approaching—a behavior sometimes called “context anxiety.”
Meta-harness design means being opinionated about the interfaces around Claude: we expect that Claude will need the ability to manipulate state (the session) and perform computation (the sandbox).
For each brain, no inference could happen until that container was provisioned; every session paid the full container setup cost up front.

Get started with Claude Managed Agents by following our docs . A running topic on the Engineering Blog is how to build effective agents and design harnesses for long-running work . A common thread across this work is that harnesses encode assumptions about what Claude can’t do on its own. However, those assumptions need to be frequently questioned because they can go stale as models improve.

As just one example, in prior work we found that Claude Sonnet 4.5 would wrap up tasks prematurely as it sensed its context limit approaching—a behavior sometimes called “context anxiety.” We addressed this by adding context resets to the harness. But when we used the same harness on Claude Opus 4.5, we found that the behavior was gone. The resets had become dead weight.

articles.title: We’ve received our first response from the Project Suncatcher prototype satellite.
articles.descEn: This week, we reached our "Hello World" milestone: the first-ever AI response from a data center class TPU in orbit.

summaryLinesEn: This week, we reached our "Hello World" milestone: the first-ever AI response from a data center class TPU in orbit.
On October 1, we launched our prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher.
Since then, we've spent the last few weeks completing our commissioning checklist, which included powering up the host and TPU trays and successfully running early machine learning tests.

On October 1, we launched our prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher. The launch marked the first step in our long-term research moonshot to explore powering AI compute in space. Since then, we've spent the last few weeks completing our commissioning checklist, which included powering up the host and TPU trays and successfully running early machine learning tests. This week, we reached our "Hello World" milestone: the first-ever AI response from a data center class TPU in orbit.

During a ground-station pass, we uplinked our first prompt to our onboard Gemma 4 open model, asking it to generate a haiku about being in space. As the satellite passed by Svalbard, Norway, the downlinked poem confirmed success:
Blue marble below Data streams in silent grace Starlight feeds my core. ✨

articles.title: Configure the ChatGPT desktop app with Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US) | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: The ChatGPT desktop app is now available on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US). This post walks through a controlled local deployment that routes model inference to Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-West) using API-mode sign-in, a managed device policy, a named AWS profile, and network restrictions, so a security team can validate it before broader use.
articles.titleEn: Configure the ChatGPT desktop app with Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US) | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: The configuration has three main steps: set up authentication, set up the ChatGPT desktop app configuration files, and then launch, initialize, and verify the deployment.
If it opens automatically or if the app has been launched previously, fully exit ChatGPT and end any lingering ChatGPT or Codex processes.
Before setting up the ChatGPT desktop app with AWS GovCloud (US), make sure your version of the ChatGPT desktop app supports Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US).

Worldwide Express (part of ShipStation Global) had built something big: approximately $5 billion in systemwide revenue, over 75 less-than-truckload (LTL) carriers and more than 130,000 customers. But that same scale had a hidden cost. Every month, $15 million in free cash flow sat frozen, locked in billing exceptions no one had resolved yet. Each one had to be chased down by hand, carrier by carrier, with its own rules to check. Worldwide Express outsourced to a team that worked cases one at a time, calling customers and carriers for each dispute. The exceptions piled up, cash stayed stuck, and every order took longer to turn into money.

Worldwide Express worked with AWS and LTM to build a multi-agentic AI solution with Amazon Bedrock that plugs directly into their transportation management system (TMS), SpeedShip. Six months after launch, the company reported a 75 percent reduction in active exceptions, a 4-week improvement in time-to-cash, $1M annual savings, and a one-time $10M free cash flow infusion.
In this post, we describe the challenge, explain how Worldwide Express designed the multi-agent solution, and share the results.

TL;DR: MonsterHouse is an interactive projection I created for Halloween. He listens to trick-or-treaters, answers in the voice of a grumpy old pirate ship and softens when visitors remember their manners. He is built on the NVIDIA Nemotron Voice Agent with NVIDIA Nemotron ASR , Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB , Magpie TTS Zeroshot and Audio2Face-3D , and he runs on a single workstation.

I wanted the kids visiting my house at Halloween to interact in a fun and unique way. The house was going to be in charge and giving out the treats, but more grumpy than scary. Somehow, my solution was to give the garage door a mouth and teach him to complain.

That became MonsterHouse: a grumpy old building with pirate stories, a fiery grin and a suspicious weakness for “please.” NVIDIA Nemotron Voice Agent supplies the conversation foundation. Nemotron Speech does the listening, Bolt E4B is the brain, NVIDIA Magpie TTS Zeroshot is the live voice, and NVIDIA Audio2Face-3D makes the wooden mouth talk.

Coding agents now build working web apps: a dashboard, a product page, a prototype that a product team wants to try. The fastest way to review that work is to open the app, use it, ask for a change, and check the result. That loop works well when the app keeps running where the agent edits it, so each change shows up in the browser within seconds. When the app must be copied out and deployed somewhere else first, every change waits for a deployment, and the review slows down to that pace.

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with your choice of agent framework and foundation model (FM). AgentCore runtime , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, runs each agent session in its own isolated microVM. With Session endpoints , you can open an app running in that session from your own browser. Session Endpoints give each session an authenticated URL that forwards each request’s HTTP method, path, query string, and body, and WebSocket connections, to the ports you allow. You can watch the page update as the agent saves each file.

In this post, you deploy a coding agent that keeps a Vite website running in its session, then open one local page with a chat on the left and the live website on the right. You ask the agent to switch the site to a dark color theme, follow its steps as they stream in, and watch the website change without a refresh. Finally, you look at what happens internally: a second port in the same session, and the requests the Session endpoint refuses.

sourceContent.headline: Managing Amazon Bedrock costs end to end: A playbook for FinOps and platform teams | Amazon Web Services
sourceContent.description: This post presents a five-stage operating model for managing Amazon Bedrock cost: attribute every dollar to an owner, make every request observable, enforce budgets, optimize platform defaults, and operate a review cadence. Written for FinOps and platform engineering teams.

The result is line_item_iam_principal entries like assumed-role/BedrockRuntimeRole/gw-alex , each carrying its user’s tags: per-user and per-tenant attribution restored behind a shared gateway.
You pass the project ID at client initialization, and its tags flow to CUR 2.0 and Cost Explorer (see Manage AI costs with Amazon Bedrock Projects ).

Cost management for generative AI is a shared responsibility between the teams that build applications and the teams accountable for cloud spend. Many teams start by comparing per-model token rates and asking application teams to shorten prompts. Those steps help, but they don’t answer the questions that finance and engineering leaders ask as usage scales: which team spent this, on which workload, and was that spend inside an approved budget?

Agentic workloads make those questions more pressing. A conversational assistant typically issues one model invocation per user turn. An agentic workflow, such as an AI coding assistant that plans a change, reads files, calls tools, and iterates, issues many invocations per task and carries a larger context on each one. Token consumption therefore scales with the degree of autonomy you grant the workflow and the size of the context it carries, rather than with the number of user interactions. Because consumption is a function of how a workload is designed and operated, cost management for generative AI is an architectural and operational discipline. Published averages are a poor substitute for your own numbers: use the AWS Pricing Calculator and the Amazon Bedrock pricing page to model rates, and use Step 2 of this post to measure what your workloads actually consume.

The fix isn’t a cheaper model or a smaller prompt. It’s an operating model: a repeatable loop that attributes every dollar to an owner, makes every request observable, alerts on and enforces budgets before overspend compounds, optimizes the platform defaults that drive most waste, and reviews the whole system on a cadence.

summaryLinesEn: 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- LiveVoice, an Austria-based live audio platform, today reported adoption across international sports events and stadiums, where organizers use the platform to deliver audio description, live translation and commentary straight to audiences’ own smartphones.

Clemens-Krauss Strasse, SALZBURG, Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- LiveVoice, an Austria-based live audio platform, today reported adoption across international sports events and stadiums, where organizers use the platform to deliver audio description, live translation and commentary straight to audiences’ own smartphones. Stadiums, arenas and organizers use LiveVoice for three things: audio description for sports events for blind and visually impaired fans, multilingual press conferences, and live audio of sports commentary. Fans need only a phone and headphones, so venues don't have to hand out, collect or maintain receivers. LiveVoice is in use at Champions League press conferences, HBL matches, and at the Red Bull Ring, which hosts Formula 1 and MotoGP race weekends.
At the Red Bull Ring in Spielberg, Austria, fans at Formula 1 and MotoGP race weekends follow live commentary on their own phones through LiveVoice, with live translation for international visitors.

Sports is one part of a wider base. Across sports venues, churches, conferences and guided tours, LiveVoice reports more than 5,000 clients, more than 200,000 events and more than 850,000 app downloads in over 100 countries.

Gen Z can’t catch a break. Entry-level jobs are vanishing ; some 40% of bosses say they plan to hire fewer grads because AI can do the job cheaper, and young workers are routinely slammed for showing up late and refusing to put in overtime for free . Cisco’s president and chief product officer Jeetu Patel isn’t buying it—he’s just handed one of the company’s biggest jobs to a 27-year-old he found hidden in the org chart “five levels” below him.
“I’ve given him unlimited tokens because he’s going to refactor code,” Patel told Fortune at a small roundtable dinner. “So I’m like, you can go, you can go nuts.”

The “him” is Padmanabhan Krishnamurthy, or “Paddy,” as Patel affectionately calls him. He joined Cisco in 2025 after the $429 billion tech giant acquired EzDubs , the real-time translation startup Krishnamurthy cofounded in 2023. And despite coming in as a former founder with CEO experience, he was, in Patel’s words, “buried away in the organization doing something unstrategic.”

MORRISVILLE, NC / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / Lenovo, the global technology powerhouse, announced that its annual global innovation event will return to CES® 2027 in Las Vegas . Hosted at Sphere and part of the CES Keynote lineup, Tech World will bring together a visionary lineup of speakers and breakthrough innovations with a first-of-its-kind immersive technology and music experience.

As well as unveiling the latest in Lenovo's innovations, Tech World will unite global technology leaders and leading voices on stage to discuss the future of AI. Together, they will explore how hybrid AI can empower people and unlock new possibilities for business and society. summaryLinesEn: Hours earlier, Intel had reported that its data center and AI business grew 78%, its fastest pace in 15 years.
The cost of insuring Intel's debt against default for five years jumped to a record 123.5 basis points on Friday, its biggest one-day move since October 2022, according to Markit data.
Intel started 2026 at $39.38, according to Yahoo Finance data, so even at $67 the stock is up about 65% this year.

articles.title: Microsoft’s AI future has fewer jobs
articles.descEn: It’s also time to name the next Elder Scrolls game, and Xbox’s architect of Forza Motorsport is leaving.
articles.titleEn: Microsoft’s AI future has fewer jobs
summaryLinesEn: This week’s voluntary exit offer arrived just months after Microsoft laid off 4,800 employees , cuts that impacted its Xbox and commercial sales teams the most.
How Nadella handles that transition will define his legacy as much as the growth and success he’s achieved over the past decade.

“Our total people costs will go down, our cost per head will go up, and my GPU per researcher will go up,” Nadella said on a podcast almost two years ago, responding to a question about AI’s impact on headcount.

articles.title: We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time
articles.descEn: Right now, we’re effectively flying blind when deploying these tools. Here’s what we need to do instead.
articles.titleEn: We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time
summaryLinesEn: The “what happened” records identify the agent (while preserving privacy) and log how humans intervened and whether agent permissions or “memory” shifted, while the “decision” records show an agent’s reasoning and levels of confidence in the actions it’s taken.
And as our recent research shows, current agent frameworks—the software that runs agents— do not reliably generate the crucial observability records we need to ensure that agents are deployed safely.

And while safety depends on monitoring, monitoring requires observability : the capacity to capture what the system did, process it into signals, and present those to humans or automated oversight systems.

localization.title: AI 에이전트의 행동을 실시간으로 모니터링하는 것이 시급하
summaryLines: "무슨 일이 있었는지" 기록은 개인정보를 보호하면서 에이전트를 식별하고 인간이 어떻게 개입했는지, 에이전트 권한 또는 "기억"이 이동했는지 여부를 기록하는 반면, "결정" 레코드는 에이전트가 취한 조치에 대한 추론과 신뢰 수준을 보여줌
그리고 최근 연구에서 알 수 있듯이 현재 에이전트 프레임워크(에이전트를 실행하는 소프트웨어)는 에이전트가 안전하게 배포되도록 보장하는 데 필요한 중요한 관찰 기록을 안정적으로 생성하지 않음
안전은 모니터링에 달려 있지만 모니터링에는 관찰 가능성이 필요함 · 즉, 시스템이 수행한 작업을 캡처하고 이를 신호로 처리하여 이를 사람이나 자동화된 감독 시스템에 제공할 수 있는 능력이 필요함

articles.title: Google's AI search problem finally shows up in the earnings report, some investors believe
articles.descEn: Google's stock dropped as much as ten percent after its quarterly earnings. Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7 billion, but search revenue grew just 12 percent, slower than expected. Google acknowledged that its fast-growing AI mode brings in less revenue than traditional search, and it is now expanding its AI mode ad program internationally.
articles.titleEn: Google's AI search problem finally shows up in the earnings report, some investors believe
summaryLinesEn: Google is doubling down on AI buildout: capital spending hit $51.4 billion in the third quarter alone, and the company expects it to "increase significantly" in 2027.
Google lost up to ten percent of its market value because an old investor fear appears to be coming true.
Google's stock dropped as much as ten percent after search revenue grew just 12 percent in the third quarter, missing the 15 percent analysts had expected.

summaryLinesEn: If AI is destined to become a central feature of both cyber offense and defense, the argument goes, businesses and governments will need to be equipped with models that are freely available and cannot be switched off remotely, unlike proprietary models from the likes of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.
At the time, the company said it was the most advanced open-weight offering outside of China.
After further refinement, Mistral now says Le Chonk is the “world’s best” open-weight model for automated coding and cybersecurity.

articles.title: I Gave My Blood to the AI Death Clock
articles.descEn: Death Clock promises to predict when you’re going to die and help you extend your time on Earth. After a month, I felt like it was sucking the life out of me.
articles.titleEn: I Gave My Blood to the AI Death Clock
summaryLinesEn: For a $69 subscription, you can get a basic blood panel that measures things like cholesterol, blood sugars, inflammation, vitamin D, and blood and organ health.
All of which led me to Death Clock, an app launched in 2024 aimed at tracking users’ health habits in an attempt to prolong their lives.
There are also nine additional tests—assessing everything from hormones and micronutrients to your thyroid—that, altogether, cost $780.

articles.titleEn: Mistral releases open weights for Mistral Large 4, providing sovereign control for the company’s ‘Le Chonk’ AI model - SiliconANGLE
summaryLinesEn: “Other labs have raised hundreds of billions to develop equivalent capabilities; in three years, Mistral raised roughly $6 billion.”
Open weights mean companies can take the model and deploy it on their own hardware, within their own firewalls, and run sensitive data without exposing it to the cloud or outside parties.
“Open source is essential to ensure state-of-the-art AI does not end up concentrated in the hands of a few actors,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Arthur Mensch.

summaryLinesEn: SpeakerDiarizer runs NVIDIA's Streaming Sortformer on Core ML alongside an Apple or Parakeet transcriber, on the same timeline: The diarizer tracks up to four speakers, even when they talk over each other.
Apple platforms already have an API for it. macOS 26 and iOS 26 introduced SpeechAnalyzer , Apple's new speech-to-text API.
Like image support in AnyLanguageModel, this goes beyond what Apple's API offers today.

articles.title: Announcing Project ProtoStar: Making Publicly Funded Science AI-Ready
articles.descEn: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
articles.titleEn: Announcing Project ProtoStar: Making Publicly Funded Science AI-Ready
summaryLinesEn: Today, we're announcing Project ProtoStar , an initiative to unlock the potential of publicly funded scientific research by making datasets, models, and code more accessible and reusable, particularly for AI-driven research.

Project ProtoStar aims to help close this gap by encouraging systematic sharing of publicly funded scientific artifacts in AI-ready formats, supported by open infrastructure and practical publishing guidance.
The resulting projects and lessons learned will help build a practical evidence base for making publicly funded science more accessible and useful.

articles.title: How Procore is powering construction analytics with OpenSharing | Databricks Blog
articles.descEn: How Procore uses Databricks OpenSharing to share hundreds of governed tables with construction companies and lift the once-a-day refresh ceiling so customers can refresh hourly.
articles.titleEn: How Procore is powering construction analytics with OpenSharing | Databricks Blog
summaryLinesEn: When a project manager, a construction executive thousands of miles away, and a superintendent on the jobsite can't see the same view of a project, decisions get made based on stale or partial information.

Doubled data availability for end customers and internal product teams, accelerating new product experiences and giving real estate facility owners, general contractors, and specialty contractors a single trusted view of every job.

Customers also need that data in their own environments, alongside everything else they run the business on (e.g. a general contractor pulling Procore data into Power BI to track workforce and personnel metrics across active jobs, or a customer joining it with their ERP and financial systems to see project execution and cost in one place).

summaryLines: 프로젝트 관리자, 수천 마일 떨어진 건설 임원, 작업 현장의 감독관이 프로젝트에 대한 동일한 보기를 볼 수 없으면 오래되거나 부분적인 정보를 기반으로 결정이 내려짐
최종 고객과 내부 제품 팀의 데이터 가용성을 두 배로 높이고, 새로운 제품 경험을 가속화하고, 부동산 시설 소유자, 일반 계약자, 전문 계약자에게 모든 작업에 대한 신뢰할 수 있는 단일 보기를 제공함
또한 고객은 비즈니스를 운영하는 다른 모든 것과 함께 자신의 환경에서 해당 데이터가 필요합니다(예 · 일반 계약업체가 Procore 데이터를 Power BI로 가져와 활성 작업 전반에 걸쳐 인력 및 인사 지표를 추적하거나 고객이 ERP 및 재무 시스템과 결합하여 프로젝트 실행 및 비용을 한 곳에서 확인하는 경우)

articles.title: Partnering with Singapore to bring frontier AI to public health
articles.descEn: Google is opening a new research hub in Singapore to deploy MedGemma and AI tools for clinicians. See how we are advancing healthcare innovation.
articles.titleEn: Partnering with Singapore to bring frontier AI to public health
summaryLinesEn: To advance scientific research, Google.org and Google DeepMind are contributing $7 million to the Philanthropy Asia Alliance’s Health for Human Potential Coalition.
Accelerating scientific breakthroughs and local research We’re establishing a Google Research hub in Singapore composed of local research scientists and software engineers.

This includes $1 million for PathGen , an AI platform that uses Google technology to help countries detect disease threats faster and share data for public health intelligence while protecting in-country data sovereignty.

articles.title: How Gemini is helping students and teachers in the classroom
articles.descEn: New studies show Gemini tutoring matches human performance and helps teachers boost student engagement. Read the full research report.
articles.titleEn: How Gemini is helping students and teachers in the classroom
summaryLinesEn: Dive into new topics with immersive explorations in the Gemini app. 15 college students share their favorite Gemini features We’re sharing 3 tips to study smarter with Gemini Notebook.

When educators used Gemini to co-design lessons, they reported feeling more creative than usual in their teaching and planning (79% with Gemini vs. 30% without Gemini) — a shift that helped transform classroom dynamics.

Together, we learned from Primary, Secondary and Vocational educators across 1,600 teachers (representing over 24,500 students ages 13-18) by collecting classroom activities and self reports on lesson planning both with and without Gemini for Education to understand how AI supports classroom dynamics, student engagement, and teacher wellbeing.

summaryLines: Gemini 앱의 몰입형 탐색을 통해 새로운 주제에 대해 알아보세요 · 15명의 대학생이 자신이 가장 좋아하는 Gemini 기능을 공유함 · Gemini Notebook을 사용하여 더욱 스마트하게 공부할 수 있는 3가지 팁을 공유함
교육자들이 Gemini를 사용하여 수업을 공동 설계했을 때 교육 및 계획에서 평소보다 더 창의적이라고 느꼈습니다(Gemini 사용 시 79%, Gemini 사용 안 함 30%) · 이는 교실 역학을 변화시키는 데 도움이 되는 변화였음
우리는 1,600명의 교사(13~18세 학생 24,500명 이상 대표)의 초등, 중등 및 직업 교육자들로부터 AI가 교실 역학, 학생 참여 및 교사 복지를 어떻게 지원하는지 이해하기 위해 Gemini for Education 유무에 관계없이 수업 계획에 대한 교실 활동과 자체 보고서를 수집하여 배웠음

summaryLinesEn: Live speech, heard and sized up by one Granite Switch model

The version number means what it means in software: fully backwards compatible with 4.1, no migration, incremental improvements under the hood.

articles.title: Americans Are Open to AI in Healthcare, but Want Humans Making Final Calls
articles.descEn: Americans are open to AI for tasks that range from scheduling to diagnoses, but they generally want human review.
articles.titleEn: Americans Are Open to AI in Healthcare, but Want Humans Making Final Calls
summaryLinesEn: A majority (60%) is uncomfortable with AI being used for healthcare tasks like diagnoses and treatments, double the share who says they’re comfortable (30%).
This builds on our previous research looking at AI’s impact on healthcare and health information.

For example, 65% of Asian adults are open to AI playing some role in decisions on health insurance claims, significantly higher than the shares of White (40%), Hispanic (45%) and Black Americans (39%) who are receptive.

articles.title: The 2026 Midterms Will Be Uniquely Difficult for Polls
articles.descEn: Polls haven't gotten worse, but fake respondents, synthetic AI surveys and election unknowns make the 2026 midterms uniquely hard to poll.
articles.titleEn: The 2026 Midterms Will Be Uniquely Difficult for Polls

sourceContent.headline: The 2026 Midterms Will Be Uniquely Difficult for Polls
sourceContent.description: Polls haven't gotten worse, but fake respondents, synthetic AI surveys and election unknowns make the 2026 midterms uniquely hard to poll.
paragraphs: And yet, many consumers expect a level of precision that polls can’t deliver.
At the same time, the rapid increase in the cost of high-quality polling has led to fewer of these polls, relative to cheaper opt-in polls.

Meanwhile, predicting who will show up to vote keeps getting harder as voting rules (when, where and how to vote) change over time and across jurisdictions, and as microtargeting by campaigns can move segments of the electorate in ways broad polls often can’t register.
Note: This analysis first appeared in The Hill on Oct. 14, 2026.

Polls are again under scrutiny, with some rushing in to proclaim their demise. But it isn’t that polls have gotten worse. Rather, a mix of factors is creating unprecedented challenges for polling and for the public trying to understand it.

Why? First, there are the perennial challenges that are consistently misunderstood. Surveys are well suited to measure beliefs and attitudes about issues, and they can capture respondents’ candidate preferences pretty accurately. But predicting who will actually turn out to vote will always be an imperfect effort, largely because people are bad at predicting their own behavior and tend to report aspirations rather than realities.

By Jake Bowman , VIP Support Lead · Oct 29, 2026 · 3 min read

Assistants have been a part of the music making process since recording studios have been around. Geoff Emerick joined EMI Studios in London (aka Abbey Road Studios) as an assistant engineer at 15 and was the Beatles’ main engineer on their album Revolver four years later. Before his entrepreneurial success, Jimmy Iovine assisted many recording sessions with artists such as John Lennon, Bruce Springsteen and Tom Petty, to name a few, in the 1970s. Their input has sped up, inspired and even challenged music producers in unique and creative ways.

But as Digital Audio Workstations (DAWs) took over, the reliance on assistants dwindled. Unlike Abbey Road, your average copy of Cubase or Pro Tools doesn’t come with someone at your beck and call to handle the tedious behind-the-scenes work your next smash hit depends on.

Azure Cloud HSM Hardware Audit Logging: Verifiable audit trails for security and compliance

Organizations running regulated and security-sensitive workloads need trusted evidence of which authenticated users performed management operations on their hardware security modules (HSMs), what actions they took, and when. Today, we are announcing Hardware Audit Logging for Azure Cloud HSM , which collects audit records generated by the HSM itself for supported management operations. Security, compliance, and operations teams can use this hardware-originated evidence for monitoring, compliance reporting, and forensic investigations.

HSMs protect some of an organization’s most sensitive cryptographic assets. The security of those assets depends not only on how keys are generated and protected, but also on how the HSM is configured and administered over time. Authentication events, user changes, policy updates, backup operations, and key lifecycle activity can all be important when teams investigate an incident, validate operational controls, or prepare evidence for an audit.

articles.title: Accelerate agentic AI with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Amazon EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts model that pairs reasoning and tool use with multimodal understanding. This post explores its architecture and use cases, then shows how to deploy it on Amazon EKS, EKS Auto Mode, and Amazon SageMaker HyperPod EKS with NVIDIA Dynamo and vLLM.
articles.titleEn: Accelerate agentic AI with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Amazon EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: NVIDIA reports 63.44 percent on Hermes Bench and 87.05 percent on LangChain agent evaluations, and 80.8 percent on the CharXiv chart-reasoning benchmark. ( technical report ) Nemotron 3.5 Super VL uses a hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE architecture, interleaving Mamba-2, attention, and expert layers.
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL supports agent workflows that combine reasoning with visual understanding: Coding: test and validate code, analyze errors, recommend fixes.
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL joins the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano , Nano Omni , Super , Ultra , and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning models already available on AWS.

articles.titleEn: You can now generate, preview, and edit documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets, and more directly in Gemini.
summaryLinesEn: We’re introducing new ways to create and refine documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets, code, and more in the Gemini app.
You can now generate, preview, and edit files right within your chat — expand to full screen to type edits directly, highlight text to ask questions, or have Gemini refine your files.

As shown in the video below, you can now ask Gemini to create a PDF study guide from your uploaded handwritten lecture notes and then you can easily manually edit, highlight specific sections to have Gemini make edits to text or visuals, and even ask further questions.

articles.title: On Facebook and Instagram, Political Ads Are Increasingly Critical of Data Centers
articles.descEn: Political ads about data centers on Facebook and Instagram have turned increasingly critical, with 57% opposed and just 3% supportive ahead of the midterms.
articles.titleEn: On Facebook and Instagram, Political Ads Are Increasingly Critical of Data Centers
summaryLinesEn: Over a period of 90 days from Jul. 27 to Oct. 24, advertisers on Facebook and Instagram spent almost $12 million on ads that mention data centers in the context of social issues, elections or politics .
The remaining 39% of recent spending has been for ads that support specific candidates.
Since late July, advertisers spent more than $1 million on political ads mentioning data centers that targeted Facebook and Instagram users in each of three states – Ohio, Wisconsin and Texas.

When engineering teams start building AI agents, the capabilities those agents need usually already exist as internal APIs.

When engineering teams start building AI agents, the capabilities those agents need usually already exist as internal APIs. Campaign creation, segment queries, delivery stats. The challenge isn’t building new functionality. The challenge is making hundreds of private APIs safely reachable by agents without exposing them to the public internet, without giving models control over identity, and without flooding context windows with hundreds of tool definitions.

MoEngage, the agentic customer engagement platform that more than 1,350 consumer brands use to deliver personalized experiences across push, email, in-app, SMS, WhatsApp, and RCS, faced exactly this problem. Behind the product sit roughly 400 internal REST APIs, built by 25 engineering teams, running in private virtual private clouds (VPCs) across seven AWS Regions. MoEngage isolates these APIs regionally to meet data residency commitments and doesn’t expose them to the public internet. The capability the agents needed was already running in production. Making it reachable, safely, was the hard part.

articles.descEn: AWS Batch quota management is a new scheduling capability you can use to divide GPU capacity into quota shares per team or project, automatically lend idle capacity across shares, and use preemption to run your highest-priority SageMaker Training jobs first, all without manual coordination.
articles.titleEn: Lend and borrow resources across teams with AWS Batch’s quota management for SageMaker Training jobs | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: If jobs arrive in a quota share that is at or above its capacity limit, AWS Batch checks whether there’s available capacity to borrow from another quota share.

These strategies determine whether idle compute is reserved until jobs arrive ( RESERVE ), lent to other quota shares that have work available ( LEND ), or both lent when idle and borrowed when the share has work that might benefit ( LEND_AND_BORROW ).

Complete the setup required to install a compatible version of the SageMaker Python SDK: Using the new quota management capabilities requires creating a Scheduling Policy that contains a quotaSharePolicy , a Service Environment that specifies its capacity limits in terms of specific instances, and a SageMaker Training job queue that is connected to both.

sourceContent.description: AWS Batch quota management is a new scheduling capability you can use to divide GPU capacity into quota shares per team or project, automatically lend idle capacity across shares, and use preemption to run your highest-priority SageMaker Training jobs first, all without manual coordination.
paragraphs: If jobs arrive in a quota share that is at or above its capacity limit, AWS Batch checks whether there’s available capacity to borrow from another quota share.

With the launch of AWS Batch support for Amazon SageMaker Training jobs, customers gained a new fully managed way to queue, schedule, and retry machine learning (ML) training workloads without building their own infrastructure. Instead, they use the queuing and scheduling features of AWS Batch. As organizations scale their artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) operations and onboard more teams, coordinating access to shared graphics processing unit (GPU) capacity can introduce additional communication, coordination, and configuration overhead for administrators. This overhead includes setting up separate queues, adjusting capacity limits, and carefully orchestrating the right workloads to get the right resources at the right time. A core value proposition of AWS Batch is helping customers increase utilization of their compute, and as training environments grow, so does the opportunity to do more with existing capacity.

Working backward from customers managing multi-team training environments, we heard a consistent request: give us a way to define allocations per team or project, share idle capacity automatically, and run our highest-priority workloads first. This request led us to build quota management , a new scheduling capability for AWS Batch. Administrators can use it to divide compute capacity into quota shares, organized by team, project, or workload. Each quota share uses configurable resource-sharing strategies that maximize GPU utilization while honoring each team’s allocation when it matters most.

This post shows how quota management works, including how to configure quota shares with lending and borrowing strategies, set up in-share preemption for priority workloads, and get started using the SageMaker Python SDK.

We recently released Claude Code , a command line tool for agentic coding. Developed as a research project, Claude Code gives Anthropic engineers and researchers a more native way to integrate Claude into their coding workflows.

Claude Code is intentionally low-level and unopinionated, providing close to raw model access without forcing specific workflows. This design philosophy creates a flexible, customizable, scriptable, and safe power tool. While powerful, this flexibility presents a learning curve for engineers new to agentic coding tools—at least until they develop their own best practices.

articles.descEn: Turn a PHP-to-Java migration from a one-time leap of faith into a measurable, repeatable process with Kiro. This post walks through a reusable engine: a mechanical discovery scanner and an eight-phase, parity-first workflow that treats the original PHP application as the specification and verifies the Java port with a parity harness.
articles.titleEn: Build a repeatable PHP-to-Java migration engine with Kiro | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: The laravel-eloquent-sample project is a working, bounded example: a read-only slice of an open source Laravel application, with the Book, Chapter, Page, and User models migrated to Spring Boot 3.4.1 on Java 21 with Maven and an in-memory H2 database.
The discipline shows in serialization: html, markdown, and text carry @JsonIgnore because the manifest recorded them in Page’s $hidden list, while Book’s description deliberately doesn’t.

When your team moves a mature PHP application to Java, you gain stronger type safety, broader library support, and more predictable scaling. A PHP codebase built over the years with Laravel, Symfony, or Doctrine carries business rules in places that are not obvious, from Eloquent traits to XML mapping files, so a structurally similar Java port can compile cleanly and still behave differently.

This post shows how to turn PHP-to-Java migration from a one-time leap of faith into a measurable, repeatable process using Kiro . Kiro is an AI integrated development environment (IDE) that pairs an AI agent with your codebase to run multi-step engineering tasks with you in the loop. The approach centers on a reusable engine: a shared methodology, a mechanical discovery scanner, and an eight-phase workflow. This engine treats the original PHP application as the specification and refuses to declare the Java port correct until a parity harness verifies it.

Familiarity with PHP (Laravel/Eloquent or Symfony/Doctrine). Java knowledge (Spring Boot, JPA) helps you review the generated output, but the engine produces idiomatic Java for you, so you don’t need to rewrite the application in Java yourself.

The approach centers on a reusable engine: a shared methodology, a mechanical discovery scanner, and an eight-phase workflow. This engine treats the original PHP application as the specification and refuses to declare the Java port correct until a parity harness verifies it.

Familiarity with PHP (Laravel/Eloquent or Symfony/Doctrine). Java knowledge (Spring Boot, JPA) helps you review the generated output, but the engine produces idiomatic Java for you, so you don’t need to rewrite the application in Java yourself.

The discipline shows in serialization: html, markdown, and text carry @JsonIgnore because the manifest recorded them in Page’s $hidden list, while Book’s description deliberately doesn’t.

With hundreds of millions of consumer profiles and thousands of brand relationships, Epsilon needed UI testing that could keep pace with rapid application changes. The solution could not create maintenance overhead for every product team.

Within Epsilon, the Agentic Platform team (50 engineers) builds shared infrastructure so other product teams can build, deploy, govern, and run AI agents safely. With this shared platform, teams get a skills-based agent builder. They also get federated identity and pre-flight authorization, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration, and cross-account provisioning. When a product team wants to adopt AI tooling, they get capabilities without additional configuration and without re-solving identity, security, browser infrastructure, or model integration on their own.

One of those managed capabilities is UI testing . With Amazon Nova Act and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser (a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore), Epsilon’s platform team could deliver resilient, intent-driven testing as a service to teams on the platform.

How SCAN Health Plan is personalizing member communications with WRITER

In the intricate, often impersonal world of healthcare, SCAN Health Plan has always charted a different course. Founded by a group of seniors who believed they could build a better, more compassionate way to navigate healthcare for their peers, this not-for-profit Medicare Advantage plan has been dedicated to one thing for nearly 50 years: keeping seniors healthy and independent. That same pioneering spirit is what drives them today as they face a new set of challenges in an industry grappling with complexity, regulatory hurdles, and a rapidly evolving technological landscape. How does an organization not only maintain but elevate the human touch in this new era?

For Trish Cox, Chief Experience Officer, and Corinne Stroum, Head of Emerging Technologies, the answer lies not in replacing human connection, but in augmenting it. It’s about leveraging the power of generative and agentic AI to empower their associates, streamline their processes, and ultimately, deliver a more empathetic, personalized, and seamless experience for their members.

Playbooks started with a simple idea — AI won’t scale prompt by prompt.

When every marketer and seller uses AI in their own corner, quality is inconsistent, costs are unpredictable, and the best workflows get trapped in one person’s private chat history. The customer experience starts to fragment, as each team creates a slightly different version of your message, your brand, and your story.

Playbooks changed that by making the best ways of working with AI repeatable and reusable across the team. WRITER customers like Clorox and Metro Bank have created more than 28,000 playbooks to personalize campaigns, optimize content for AI visibility, generate account insights, and more.

articles.title: Play the future of mobile gaming: Neural Dawn now available to download

summaryLinesEn: Neural graphics are changing what’s possible, using AI-based techniques to reduce traditional rendering workloads and free up graphics performance, so developers can devote more of their graphics budget to lighting, shadows, motion, and more cinematic environments.
Arm Total Design for Physical AI brings silicon, software, safety, security, validation, and more into one collaborative ecosystem to help build, validate, and scale full-stack solutions on Arm.

Local Network Permission : This permission is restricted to apps that need it for core functionality when device pickers are insufficient. Apps targeting Android 17 or higher (API 37+) must submit a Play Console declaration to use this permission.

Nebius Group N.V. NBIS and IREN Limited IREN are capitalizing on the rapidly growing demand for AI computing infrastructure. The increasing adoption of generative AI, agentic AI and inference applications is driving substantial demand for high-performance GPUs, data centers and scalable cloud platforms. However, the availability of power, land and data center capacity remains a major constraint, as physical infrastructure takes years to develop while AI workloads continue to expand rapidly. Growing demand from hyperscalers, AI developers and enterprises, coupled with limited near-term computing capacity, is creating significant growth opportunities for AI infrastructure providers and supporting favorable pricing trends.

Nebius is focused on building a full-stack AI cloud platform, combining GPU infrastructure, software and services to support AI-native companies, enterprises and other customers. The company is expanding its computing capacity while pursuing flexible contracting models and asset-light partnerships to capitalize on increasing demand.

articles.title: AI buildout hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecasts
articles.descEn: Microsoft and Alphabet both reported capital expenditures that fell short of estimates, adding to concern over the cost of the AI buildout.
articles.titleEn: AI buildout hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecasts
summaryLinesEn: In Meta's earnings report last week, the company said it expects full-year capex of $135 billion to $145 billion, raising the bottom of the range from $130 billion.
Microsoft's Hood said Wednesday that she sees capital spending accelerating in the first half of 2027 thanks to higher component costs and the delayed deliveries.

articles.title: I Put a Bunch of AI Agents in Charge of a Fantasy Soccer Team. They’re Not Better Than Humans—Yet
articles.descEn: To experiment with AI’s predictive skills, I let Codex loose on a fantasy team. It tried to bench Erling Haaland at first, but it soon learned the error of its ways.
articles.titleEn: I Put a Bunch of AI Agents in Charge of a Fantasy Soccer Team. They’re Not Better Than Humans—Yet
summaryLinesEn: I tried increasing the number of agents to more than 100, hoping this would make the system smarter still, but it didn’t change much besides running up my API bill.

According to Haifeng Xu , a computer scientist at the University of Chicago who studies the uses of AI in market situations, newer models may be even better at making predictions because they’re able to consume and analyze huge amounts of real-world information, and they’re able to orchestrate more complex systems for their guesses.

It’s one of a number of benchmarks designed to test AI’s future-gazing capabilities; another, Prediction Arena , from researchers at Harvard University and a company called Arcada Labs, recently gave frontier models $10,000 to wager on prediction markets over 57 days.

summaryLines: 시스템이 더욱 스마트해지길 바라면서 에이전트 수를 100개 이상으로 늘려 보았지만 API 비용이 많이 소모되는 것 외에는 크게 바뀌지 않았음
시장 상황에서 AI의 사용을 연구하는 시카고 대학의 컴퓨터 과학자인 Haifeng Xu에 따르면, 최신 모델은 엄청난 양의 실제 정보를 소비하고 분석할 수 있으며 추측을 위해 더 복잡한 시스템을 조율할 수 있기 때문에 예측에 훨씬 더 뛰어날 수 있음
이는 AI의 미래 예측 능력을 테스트하기 위해 설계된 여러 벤치마크 중 하나임 · Harvard University의 연구원과 Arcada Labs라는 회사의 또 다른 Prediction Arena는 최근 프론티어 모델에게 57일 동안 예측 시장에 베팅할 수 있도록 10,000달러를 제공함

articles.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a ‘significant leap’ in cybersecurity
articles.descEn: Google has launched Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier model that the company says offers “significant gains” in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity.
articles.titleEn: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a ‘significant leap’ in cybersecurity
summaryLinesEn: It will launch at the same competitive introductory price as Argon, at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
Google has released its latest frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, offering “significant gains” in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity.
In an announcement on Wednesday , Google highlights Carbon’s top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark, with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra trailing behind.

articles.title: Google opens Android development to third-party AI agents and unveils new Gemini APIs
articles.descEn: Google is opening up Android Studio to third-party AI agents. Through a new "Bring Your Own Agent" feature, the IDE now supports more than 40 coding agents, including Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex. Google says new terminal tools also help agents finish UI tasks 77 percent faster while using up to three times fewer tokens. Android development is becoming agent-centric too.
articles.titleEn: Google opens Android development to third-party AI agents and unveils new Gemini APIs
summaryLinesEn: Google and hardware maker XREAL also unveiled the XREAL AURA, a $1,099 pair of smart glasses running Android XR that displays virtual workspaces and uses Gemini to analyze the real-world environment.

Ad New terminal tools and specialized skills cut token usage for coding agents Google expanded the Android CLI command-line tool for developers who run their agents in the terminal or in CI pipelines.
It evaluates language models on multi-day development projects based on functionality, time spent, and cost.

articles.title: Macmillan Staff Say the Publisher Threw a Party for a Workplace AI Assistant That Was Later Killed
articles.descEn: Workers tell WIRED that NOA—or “No Ordinary Assistant”—was unhelpful. Bestselling authors also say AI is ruining their relationships with Big Five publishers.
articles.titleEn: Macmillan Staff Say the Publisher Threw a Party for a Workplace AI Assistant That Was Later Killed
summaryLinesEn: Brandon Sanderson, for instance, publishes some of his fantasy novels through Tor Books, an imprint of Macmillan, but raised more than $15 million from his readers on Kickstarter to publish four books on his own in 2022.
In an email to staff, NOA was introduced as an AI chatbot developed by the German software company Chaptr, which is “backed” by Holtzbrinck, Macmillan’s parent company.
Ostensibly, this means NOA was a closed-loop enterprise tool that did not retain or share data for model training.

articles.title: AI execs may be too out of touch to build for the general public
articles.descEn: Tech leaders are flaunting how out of touch they are when they brag about using AI to connect with their families.
articles.titleEn: AI execs may be too out of touch to build for the general public
summaryLinesEn: “The average American I think has, it’s fewer than three friends, three people they’d consider friends, and the average person has demand for meaningfully more, I think it’s like 15 friends,” Zuckerberg said last year on a podcast .

"She thought it was perfect."www.nytimes.com/2026/10/25/s… Perhaps Mayer drew so much backlash because we have repeatedly observed sheltered billionaires suggest that we outsource childrearing — one of life’s greatest tests of patience, humility, and kindness — to a computer that is incapable of understanding human emotion.

In an interview about her new app Dazzle, an AI assistant that learns from your camera roll, Mayer poses what she believes is an impressive flex for the product: it helped her come up with three bullet points about her ten-year-old daughter for a birthday presentation at school, describing her as “empathetic, creative, and an animal lover.”

localization.title: AI 임원은 일반 대중을 위해 구축하기에는 너무 멀리 떨어져 있을 수 있음
summaryLines: 저커버그는 지난해 팟캐스트에서 "내가 생각하는 평균적인 미국인은 친구가 3명도 안 되는 것 같 · 친구라고 생각하는 사람은 3명이며, 평균적인 사람은 의미 있게 더 많은 친구를 요구함 · 내 생각엔 15명의 친구와 같다"고 말함
"그녀는 그것이 완벽하다고 생각함" · www.nytimes.com/2026/10/25/s… 아마도 메이어는 보호받는 억만장자들이 인간의 감정을 이해할 수 없는 컴퓨터에 자녀 양육(인내, 겸손, 친절에 대한 인생의 가장 큰 시험 중 하나)을 아웃소싱한다고 제안한 것을 반복적으로 관찰했기 때문에 그렇게 많은 반발을 받았을 것임
카메라 롤에서 학습하는 AI 비서인 그녀의 새로운 앱인 Dazzle에 대한 인터뷰에서 Mayer는 제품에 대한 인상적인 유연성이라고 생각하는 것을 제시함 · 이는 그녀가 학교에서 생일 프레젠테이션을 위해 열 살 된 딸에 대해 세 가지 중요 사항을 제시하는 데 도움이 되었으며 그녀를 "공감력이 있고 창의적이며 동물 애호가"라고 묘사함

articles.title: Voice AI in vogue: Nvidia releases new open transcription model
articles.descEn: Nvidia just released a free speech-to-text model that can transcribe up to 40 languages, but it only works on recordings, not live audio, so it’s a big step for meeting and medical transcription tools while still leaving real-time use to rivals like ElevenLabs.
articles.titleEn: Voice AI in vogue: Nvidia releases new open transcription model
summaryLinesEn: Nvidia on Wednesday released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe , a free, open-weight model that transcribes audio in up to 40 languages.

Nvidia’s latest voice entry comes during a busy period of AI voice releases: Mistral shipped Voxtral 3 earlier this month; ElevenLabs launched Realtime for instant speech in voice agents; and Salesforce released Launa-Omni, its voice model.
Provides movers and shakers with the info they need to start their day.

articles.title: With AI writing the code, entrepreneurial thinking is now what counts most for newcomers at Anthropic
articles.descEn: Anthropic manager Felix Rieseberg says the classic coding interview is dead because Claude now solves small programming tasks better than job candidates do. He'd rather see prototypes that show taste, empathy, and principled thinking, since in his words, "hunger beats tenure." That sounds empowering, but it pushes the bar for newcomers toward entrepreneurial thinking and assumes a hustle mentality not everyone brings to the job.
articles.titleEn: With AI writing the code, entrepreneurial thinking is now what counts most for newcomers at Anthropic
summaryLinesEn: Most universities barely teach those skills, and companies have traditionally expected them from experienced product managers or founders.
Why newcomers spot the problems veterans stopped seeing Rieseberg argues that newcomers have a structural advantage because they notice problems that long-time employees accepted as givens years ago.
You had to work your way up a rigid hierarchy before management trusted you to actually build something.

articles.title: AI agents hacked Anthropic, maker of arguably the most capable AI models for cyberdefense
articles.descEn: Cybersecurity startup Cathedral used AI agents to break into Anthropic's internal systems through third-party software as part of a bug bounty program. Anthropic confirmed access to sales, HR, and IT data but disputes how deep the breach went. The incident shows how vulnerable even leading AI labs are through their external software dependencies.
articles.titleEn: AI agents hacked Anthropic, maker of arguably the most capable AI models for cyberdefense
summaryLinesEn: Ad Anthropic confirmed that the researchers accessed a limited set of sales, human resources, and IT systems, including contact information for some customers and partners along with basic user account data.
AI agents are changing how cyberattacks work, and this breach shows how fast the shift is happening.
The incident shows a growing threat: AI agents can now probe corporate networks around the clock at minimal cost, and even Anthropic isn't safe.
